source_text: long, long ago god created the heavens and the earth.
target_text: uru-uru tèka, ama lamatua paj'aj'i dedha-liru dènge rai-haha.

source_text: when he began to create the earth, it was shapeless and completely desolate/chaotic. darkness covered the deep water that surrounded the earth. and the spirit of god was hovering over the water.
target_text: lod'o rai-haha j'aj'i mèka, aa'i-aa'i dhae mèci mèka. dhu abhu, èi. aa maroga aatu-aatu saguru nare ne. ka roh lamatua lela ètu dedha èi èèna.

source_text: god said, i want light to shine! and light shone.
target_text: hèia ama lamatua peka, hud'i ku dènge saraa. ropa peka nare sèmi ne'e, ka saraa j'aj'i dènge ka.

source_text: god was pleased with the light. then he made the light to shine in some places, and in other places there was still darkness.
target_text: ropa nèdhi saraa ne, d'ara na karej'e, lula ngaa dhu na ad'u, mema be'a. hèia na hag'e eele saraa nèti maroga, sèna ka èci-èci ka dènge taa na.

source_text: he gave to the light the name ‘day', and he gave to the darkness the name ‘night'. after that, there was an evening which was followed by a morning. he called that whole period of time ‘the first day'.
target_text: ka pangare saraa ne ‘mèu', aa maroga na ‘mèda'. ne'e ne, lod'o ka èci kèna.

source_text: then god said, i command that there be an empty space like a huge dome to separate the water that is above it from the water on the earth that is below it! and that is what happened. god gave to the space the name ‘sky'.
target_text: hèia ama lamatua lii hari, na peka, hud'i dènge ku era talele, sèna ka hag'e eele èi. nèti èèna ka, èi re dedha, aa abhu kahèi èi re haha. ropa peka nare sèmi èèna, hèia èi b'agi dènge mi dua.

source_text: then there was another evening, which was followed by another morning. he called that period of time ‘the second day'.
target_text: ka na pangare èi re dedha na, ‘liru'. ne'e ne, lod'o ka dua kèna.

source_text: then god said, i want the water that is below the sky to come together, and dry ground to appear and rise above the water. and that is what happened.
target_text: hèia ama lamatua peka hari, aku nèngu na, èi re haha hud'i pakaboko ku mi ca era, sèna ka abhu rai kamango. ropa padhai lii nare sèmi ne'e, j'aj'i dènge ka rai mango.

source_text: god gave to the ground the name ‘earth', and he gave to the water that came together the name ‘oceans'. god was pleased with the earth and the oceans.
target_text: ka era rai mango, na pangare na ‘rai-dedha'; aa era èi dhu kaboko èèna, na pangare na ‘dhasi'. ropa nèdhi aa'i-aa'i ne, d'ara na karej'e, lula ngaa dhu na ad'u, mema be'a.

source_text: then god said, i want the earth to produce plants, including plants that will produce seeds and trees that will produce fruit. each kind of tree will bear its own kind of fruit.
target_text: ka ama lamatua lii hari, peka na, rai hud'i pamamuri ku rupa-rupa ana aaj'u. sèna ka abhu aj'u dhu hua, dhu dènge lamusi, aa dhu dènge rèu mangèru. sèna ka aj'u-aj'u se, hua-hela madhutu rupa rèngu. ropa padhai lii nare sèmi ne'e, j'aj'i dènge ka ana aaj'u aa'i-aa'i ra.

source_text: then plants grew on the earth; each kind of plant began to produce its own kind of seed.
target_text: ètu dedha-rai, ana aaj'u se hua-hela ka madhutu rupa rèngu. ropa nèdhi aa'i-aa'i se, d'ara na karej'e, lula ngaa dhu na ad'u, mema be'a.

source_text: then there was another evening which was followed by another morning. god called that period of time ‘the third day'.
target_text: ne'e ne, lod'o ka tèlu kèna.

source_text: then god said, i want a sun, a moon, and many stars to shine in the sky. the sun will shine in the daytime and the moon and stars will shine during the nighttime. by the changes in their appearance they will indicate the various seasons or, the times for special celebrations, and will enable people to know when days and years begin. i want them also to be like lights in the sky that will shine on the earth. and that is what happened.
target_text: hèia ama lamatua lii hari, aku nèngu na, re bèka dedha, hud'i abhu ku mèdha dhu saraa, ho pasaraa rai-haha ne. hud'i abhu mèdha dhu pasaraa re mèu, aa abhu kahèi dhu pasaraa re mèda. rèngu aa'i-aa'i se, j'aj'i tadha, ho sèna ka bisa ige lod'o, hèru, dènge tèu. ropa padhai lii nare sèmi ne'e, mèdha dhu heo aa'i-aa'i ra j'aj'i dènge ka.

source_text: god made two of them that were like big lights. the bigger one, the sun, shines during the day and the smaller one, the moon, shines during the night. he also made the stars.
target_text: ka na tao ka mèdha kapai dua dhu pasaraa rai-haha. dhu kapai risi, pasaraa re mèu; aa dhu ako ana iiki, pasaraa re mèda. aa na tao hua-hètu kahèi.

source_text: god set all of them in the sky to shine on the earth,
target_text: na tèke mèdha dhu saraa sèra ètu dedha-liru, sèna ka loti mai asa rai-haha.

source_text: to rule the day and the night, and to separate the light of the daytime from the darkness of the nighttime. god was pleased with these things he had made.
target_text: ka mèdha se, pasaraa ka re mèu, aa pasaraa re mèda. dènge j'ara ne'e, na hag'e eele saraa nèti maroga. ropa nèdhi aa'i-aa'i se, d'ara na karej'e, lula ngaa dhu na ad'u, mema be'a.

source_text: then there was another evening which was followed by another morning. he called that period of time ‘the fourth day'.
target_text: ne'e ne, lod'o ka èpa kèna.

source_text: then god said, i want many creatures to live in all the oceans, and i also want birds to fly in the sky above the earth.
target_text: hèia ama lamatua padhai lii hari, peka na, hud'i abhu ku ae-ae dhu mamuri ètu d'ara èi. dènge hud'i abhu ku rupa-rupa manu-bhui dhu lela ètu dedha rai-haha ne.

source_text: so god created huge sea creatures and every other kind of creature that moves in the water, and caused them to live in all the oceans. he also created many kinds of birds. god was pleased with all those creatures.
target_text: ka na tao ka i'a aa'i-aa'i dènge badha kapai dhu mamuri ètu d'ara èi. na paj'aj'i kahèi manu-bhui aa'i-aa'i. ropa nèdhi aa'i-aa'i se, d'ara na karej'e, lula ngaa dhu na ad'u, mema be'a.

source_text: god blessed them. he said, produce offspring and become very numerous. i want the creatures in the water to live in all the oceans, and birds also to become very numerous. and that is what happened.
target_text: ka na padhai lii ho sèna ka hia berkat mi aa'i-aa'i dhu mamuri, peka na, i'a se, hud'i laa bèba-kacanga sèna ka papènu èi ètu mia-mia. aa manu-bhui, asa tabha kahèi.

source_text: then there was another evening that was followed by another morning. he called that period of time ‘the fifth day'.
target_text: ne'e ne, lod'o ka lèmi kèna.

source_text: then god said, i want various kinds of creatures to appear on the earth. there will be many kinds of ◄livestock/domestic animals►, creatures that scurry across the ground, and large wild animals. and that is what happened. god made all kinds of wild animals and ◄livestock/domestic animals► and all kinds of creatures that scurry across the ground. god was pleased with all these creatures.
target_text: ka ama lamatua peka hari, na, hud'i abhu ku rupa-rupa badha dhu mamuri ètu rai-dedha. sèmi: badha-manu dhu ani, badha hui, dènge badha dhu rod'o, èci-èci ka dènge rupa na. ropa padhai lii nare sèmi ne'e, badha aa'i-aa'i ra j'aj'i dènge ka. ropa nèdhi aa'i-aa'i se, d'ara na karej'e, lula ngaa dhu na ad'u, mema be'a.

source_text: then god said, now we will make human beings that will be like us in many ways. i want them to rule over the fish in the sea, over the birds, over all the ◄livestock/domestic animals►, and over all the other creatures that scurry across the ground.
target_text: ka ama lamatua peka hari, aku nèngu na, hua iia, mai ta paj'aj'i dhèu, madhutu rupa èdhi. hud'i laa ra leru dènge ator i'a aa'i-aa'i ètu d'ara dhasi, manu-bhui aa'i-aa'i ètu dedha-liru, badha-manu dhu ani, dènge badha leo aa'i-aa'i ra dhu mamuri ètu rai-haha ne.

source_text: so god created human beings that were like him in many ways. he made them to be like himself. he created some to be male and some to be female.
target_text: hèia na paj'aj'i dhèu rai-haha ne madhutu rupa na. na paj'aj'i si, dhèu mone dènge dhèu bhèni.

source_text: god blessed them, saying, produce many children, who will live all over the earth and rule over it. i want them to rule over the fish and the birds and over all creatures that scurry across the ground.
target_text: ka na padhai lii ho sèna ka hia berkat mi rèngu, aku nèngu na, miu hud'i bèba-kacanga ku, sèna ka pea papènu rai-haha ne, ho mi ator ne. ja'a hia miu koasa, sèna ka mi ator i'a, manu-bhui, dènge badha-manu aa'i-aa'i ra ètu rai-haha ne.

source_text: god said to the humans, listen! i have given you all the plants that produce seeds, all over the earth, and all the trees that have seeds in their fruit. all these things are for you to eat.
target_text: mi nanene paie-iie! ja'a hia miu rupa-rupa nganga'a ètu rai-haha ne'e. sèmi: ana aaj'u dhu dènge hua, dhu dènge lamusi, aa dhu dènge rèu mangèru.

source_text: i have given all the green plants to all the wild animals and to the birds and to all the creatures that scurry across the ground, to everything that breathes, for them to eat. and that is what happened.
target_text: ja'a hia rupa-rupa ana aaj'u kahèi sèna ka j'aj'i nganga'a badha. nganga'a hia badha-manu dhu ani, badha hui, badha dhu rod'o, dènge manu-bhui. ropa padhai lii nare sèmi ne'e, nganga'a badha sèra aa'i-aa'i ra j'aj'i dènge ka.

source_text: god was pleased with everything that he had made. truly, it was all very good. then there was another evening, that was followed by another morning. he called that period of time ‘the sixth day'.
target_text: ropa nèdhi aa'i-aa'i se, d'ara na karej'e, lula ngaa dhu na ad'u, mema be'a. ne'e ne, lod'o ka èna kèna.

source_text: that is the way god created the heavens and the earth.
target_text: dènge j'ara sèmi èèna ka, ama lamatua paj'aj'i dedha-liru, rai-haha, dènge isi ra aa'i-aa'i.

source_text: by the time it was the seventh day, god had finished the work of creating everything, so he did not work any more on that day.
target_text: ropa na sab'a èle, asa bèli èèna, lèke dènge lod'o ka pidhu. hèia na ae nèti sasab'a-la'a na.

source_text: god blessed each seventh day, and he set those days apart to be special days, because on the seventh day god did not work any more, after finishing all his work of creating everything.
target_text: dènge j'ara ne'e, na tao lod'o ka pidhu ne, lod'o dhu kapai risi nèti lod'o dhu leo sèra. na tao sèmi èèna, lula na pa'èle aa'i le sasab'a na, ka ètu d'ara lod'o ka pidhu na, na ae.

source_text: that is how god created the heavens and the earth. god, whose name is yahweh, made the heavens and the earth.
target_text: d'ai sange ne'e ka, lii lolo ama lamatua paj'aj'i dedha-liru dènge rai-haha ne. lod'o ama lamatua heka paj'aj'i dedha-liru dènge rai-haha èèna,

source_text: at first there were no plants growing, because yahweh god had not yet caused rain to fall on the ground. furthermore, there was no one to till the ground for planting crops. instead, mist rose up from the ground, so that it watered the surface of the ground.
target_text: dhae abhu mèka ana aaj'u, lula na papuru mèka èj'i. taa èèna, dhoka sèb'u èi di, mai nèti d'ara rai ho pabasa rai re dedha. aa abhu mèka dhèu rai-haha dhu tao oka-tedhe.

source_text: then yahweh god took some soil and formed a man. he breathed into the man's nostrils his own breath that gives life, and as a result the man became a living person.
target_text: èle èèna ka, ama lamatua nare rai ciki, ka na paj'aj'i dhèu rai-haha. hèia na tiu a'ae na asa d'ara sahènga dhèu na, ka na mamuri dènge ka.

source_text: yahweh god made a park/garden in a place named eden, which was east of the land of canaan, and he put there the man that he had created.
target_text: hèia ama lamatua bhoke oka cue ètu rai eden, re bèka dhimu. hèia na hia dhèu ne pea ètu d'ara oka na.

source_text: yahweh god also put there every kind of tree that is beautiful to see and that produced fruit that was good to eat. he also placed in the middle of the park/garden a tree whose fruit would enable those who ate it to live forever. he also placed there another tree whose fruit would enable those who ate it to know what actions were good to do and what actions were evil to do.
target_text: ètu d'ara oka èèna, na pamamuri rupa-rupa aj'u dhu be'a, dhu dhèu bisa ra'a. aa na pamamuri kahèi aj'u dua kapua ètu talora aae oka èèna. ladhe dhèu ra'e hua nèti aj'u èci, na mamuri taa-taa. aa ladhe dhèu ra'e hua nèti aj'u èci hari, ne'a hag'e mia dhu be'a, aa mia dhu karehe.

source_text: a river flowed from eden to provide water for the park/garden. outside of eden, the river divided into four rivers.
target_text: ètu era èèna, abhu loko èci dhu hae nèti d'ara oka èèna. loko èèna, èpa kacanga.

source_text: the name of the first river is pishon. that river flows through all the land of havilah, where there is gold.
target_text: kacanga ka èci na, ngara na pison. nèngu ka dhu hae pale-lème rai hawila dhu abhu hualaa ae-ae.

source_text: that gold ◄is very pure/has no impurities in it►. there is also a sweet-smelling gum called bdellium, and valuable stones called onyx.
target_text: ètu era èèna ka, abhu poe-pai, aj'u dhu raa na hèu mèngi, dènge hadhu kale'e.

source_text: the name of the second river is gihon. that river flows through all the land of cain.
target_text: kacanga ka dua, ngara na gihon. kacanga ne, hae pale-lème rai kus.

source_text: the name of the third river is tigris. it flows east of the city of asshur. the name of the fourth river is euphrates.
target_text: kacanga ka tèlu, ngara na tigris. kacanga ne'e ka, j'aj'i mi too rai asyur re ca bèka dhimu. kacanga ka èpa, ngara na efrat.

source_text: yahweh god took the man and put him in eden park/garden to till/cultivate it and take care of it.
target_text: ka ama lamatua hia dhèu pea ètu d'ara eden, ho na ladhe-leru oka èèna.

source_text: but yahweh said to him, you must not eat the fruit of the tree that will enable you to know what actions are good to do and what actions are evil to do. if you eat any fruit from that tree, on that day your relationship with me will end. but i will permit you to eat the fruit of any of the other trees in the park/garden.
target_text: hèia na hia paredha mi dhèu ne, aku nèngu na, hua aaj'u aa'i-aa'i ètu d'ara oka ne, èu bisa mu'a. te ngaa èci dhu èu bisa boe mu'a. nuka hua nèti aj'u dhu ne'a hag'e mia dhu be'a, aa mia dhu karehe. ladhe mu'a, èu madhe dènge.

source_text: then yahweh god said, it is not good for this man to be alone. so i will make someone who will be a suitable partner for him.
target_text: ka ama lamatua tuhu haru lii na, aku nèngu na, babe'a na aad'o, ladhe dhèu ne mamuri mesa na. de ja'a neo paj'aj'i hia ne, anga ca dhèu dhu pamèci dènge ne.

source_text: yahweh god had taken some soil and had formed from it all kinds of animals and birds, and he brought them to the man to hear what names he would give them. then the man gave names to all the kinds of livestock and birds and wild animals, but none of these creatures was a partner that was suitable for the man.
target_text: lod'o èèna, ama lamatua nare rai ciki, ka na tao rupa-rupa badha dènge manu-bhui. hèia na pangèd'u si asa dhèu ne, sèna ka na pangare si. ka dhèu ne pangare badha se dènge manu-bhui aa'i-aa'i ra, èci-èci ka dènge ngara ra. te ngaa dhèu ne abhu mèka anga dhu pamèci dènge nèngu.

source_text: so yahweh god caused the man to fall into a deep sleep. while the man was sleeping, yahweh took out one of the man's ribs. then he immediately closed the opening in his body and healed it.
target_text: hèia ama lamatua pabhèj'i luu dhèu ne'e. ropa na bhèj'i, ama lamatua nare rui karasa na calaa, ka na pakateme hari nu'a deo na.

source_text: yahweh then made a woman from the rib that he had taken from the man's body, and he brought her to the man.
target_text: nèti rui ne, na paj'aj'i bhèni ca dhèu. hèia na pangèd'u bhèni ne mi dhèu èèna.

source_text: the man exclaimed, wow! this is truly ◄someone like me/what i was looking for! ► she is truly from my bones and from my flesh. so i will call her woman, because she was taken from me, a man.
target_text: ropa ladhe nèdhi bhèni ne, ka dhèu na peka, aku nèngu na, waaa! ne'e ne ku! sèmi ne'e ku, heka pamèci dènge ja'a kèna! rui na, sama èci èèna ka dènge rui ja'a. aa isi na, sama kahèi dènge isi ja'a. lula nèngu ne, j'aj'i nèti dhèu mone, nèti èèna ka ja'a pangare ne, ‘dhèu bhèni'.

source_text: the first woman was taken from the man's body, so that is why when a man and a woman marry, they must leave their parents. the man will join very closely to his wife, so that the two of them will be as though they are one person.
target_text: nèti èèna ka, dhèu mone hud'i tèke eele ku ina-ama na, ho la'e mamuri d'ara èci dènge dhèu èmu-kamali na, lula dua ra, j'aj'i le èci.

source_text: although the man and his wife were naked, they were not ashamed about that.
target_text: lod'o èèna, dua ra dhu dènge boe mèdha-papake, te ngaa ra makae boe.

source_text: the snake was more cunning than all the other wild animals that yahweh god had made. one day satan gave to the snake the ability to talk to the woman. the snake said to her, did god really say to you, ‘do not eat the fruit from any of the trees in the park/garden'?
target_text: nèti badha aa'i-aa'i dhu ama lamatua paj'aj'i ètu rai-haha ne, mege ka dhu mèu risi kapod'e-kabèli. ca lod'o, mege karèi bhèni na, aku nèngu na, tare'a, do? ama lamatua kai miu baku mi'a hua aaj'u aa'i-aa'i ètu d'ara oka ne'e.

source_text: the woman replied, what god said was, ‘do not eat the fruit from the tree that is in the middle of the park/garden or touch it. if you do that, you will die. but you can eat fruit from any of the other trees. '
target_text: ka bhèni na b'ala, aad'o! ji'i bisa nga'a! dhodhoka aj'u ca kapua ètu talora oka ne, ama lamatua kai, baku nga'a hua na. na peka na, ji'i baku nga'a, aa baku g'ag'e hua èèna kahèi, te aad'o na, ji'i madhe!

source_text: the snake said to the woman, no, you will certainly not die. god said that
target_text: te ngaa mege na dhaa, aku nèngu na, waa! sèmi boe èèna! miu se madhe boe!

source_text: only because he knows that when you eat fruit from that tree, you will understand new things. it will be as though your eyes are opened met, and you will know what is good to do and what is evil to do, just as god does.
target_text: ama lamatua mema kai tare'a sèmi èèna, lula dhu ne'a le, ladhe mi'e hua aaj'u èèna, miu j'aj'i d'èlu-mèu sèmi nèngu. ho èèna na me'a mia dhu be'a, aa mia dhu karehe.

source_text: the woman saw that the fruit on that tree was good to eat, and it was very beautiful, and she desired it because she thought it would make her wise. so she picked some of the fruit and ate it. then she gave some to her husband, and he ate it.
target_text: aa bhèni ne ladhe na aj'u ne be'a titu kèna, dènge hua na ele boe kee. na ngee, ladhe ja'a ku'a hua aj'u ne'e, ja'a d'èlu-mèu. hèia puu nare ka hua aj'u èèna, ka na'e. na'e nare, nèti hia dhèu èmu na, ka na'a kahèi.

source_text: immediately it was as though their eyes were opened, and they realized that they were naked, so they were ashamed. so they picked some fig leaves and fastened them together to make clothes for themselves.
target_text: ra'a rare ka, heka re'a na rèngu dhu pake boe mèdha dhu hutu ua rèngu. nèti èèna ka, ra lui rèu aj'u ho pa'abhe era makae rèngu.

source_text: late that afternoon, when a cool breeze was blowing, they heard the sound/footsteps of yahweh as he was walking in the park/garden. so the man and his wife hid themselves among the bushes in the park/garden, so that yahweh god would not see them.
target_text: d'ai lod'o nihia, dua ra tadèngi lii core haga ama lamatua ètu d'ara oka èèna. ka dua ra rai lasi lu'u asa ca bèka aj'u, sèna ka lamatua baku nèdhi si.

source_text: but yahweh god called to the man, saying to him, why are you trying to hide from me?
target_text: te ngaa ama lamatua paroa mi dhèu mone èèna, aku nèngu na, adam! èu ètu mia?

source_text: the man replied, i heard the sound of your footsteps/walking in the garden, and i was naked, so i was afraid and i hid myself.
target_text: hèia mone na dhaa, ja'a tadèngi lii lamatua ètu ne'e. te ngaa ja'a makae, lula ja'a pake boe mèdha ètu ua. nèti èèna ka, ja'a rai pahuni iisi.

source_text: god said, how did you find out you were naked rhq? it must be because you ate some of the fruit from the tree that i told you, ‘do not eat its fruit. ' rhq
target_text: ka lamatua peka na, cee ka dhu peka, na èu dhu pake boe mèdha-papake? de tasamia? tatu èu mu'a le hua aj'u dhu ja'a kai na, sina ma?

source_text: the man said, you gave me this woman to be with me. she is the one who gave me some of the fruit from that tree, and so i ate it.
target_text: ka na b'ala, peka na, bhèni dhu èu hia ho pa'anga dènge ja'a èèna, ka dhu hia ja'a ku'a!

source_text: then yahweh god said to the woman, why did you do such a thing? the woman replied, i ate some of the fruit because the snake deceived me.
target_text: hèia ama lamatua peka dènge bhèni na, aku nèngu na, nga tao ka, èu ad'u madha j'ara èèna? ka bhèni ne dhaa, peka na, te mege ne ka dhu ag'o ja'a! nèti èèna ka, ja'a ku'a.

source_text: then yahweh god said to the snake, because you did this, of all the livestock and the wild animals, i will curse/punish you alone. as a result, you and all other snakes will scurry across the ground on your bellies, and so what you eat will have dirt on it as long as you live.
target_text: èle èèna ka, ama lamatua dhoo mege èèna, aku nèngu na, ja'a huku èu, lula tatao èu. nèti badha aa'i-aa'i, dhoka èu di dhu abhu huku sèmi ne'e. mulai nèti deo ne'e toke èu madhe, èu dhoka rod'o dènge kakara, aa mu'a ètu rai di.

source_text: and i will cause you and the woman to act in a hostile way toward each other, and i will cause your brood and her descendants to act hostilely toward each other. you will strike at the heel of one descendant of hers, but he will strike your head.
target_text: ja'a tao sèna ka, èu loe boe pamusu dènge bhèni ne. aa ana-èpu miu dua mi sèmi èèna kahèi. ana-èpu èu, èèna na kadhi hui tèdhu dhèu. te ngaa ca dhèu nèti ana-èpu bhèni ne, èèna na dhedhe palaho kètu èu.

source_text: then yahweh said to the woman, you will have great pain when you give birth to children; you will suffer great pain as your children are being born dou. you will greatly desire your husband to show affection for you, but he will rule over you.
target_text: èle èèna ka, ama lamatua peka dènge bhèni ne, èèna na, ja'a pasusa tabha èu, ropa èu dènge babia; lod'o mora iisi, èu asa tabha j'èra. masi ka sèmi èèna, d'ara èu d'èi taruu dhèu èmu èu, aa nèngu ka dhu ator èu.

source_text: then yahweh said to the man, you heeded what your wife said, and you ate some of the fruit of the tree concerning which i commanded you saying, ‘do not eat it. ' so i will make it difficult to grow things in the ground because of what you did. you will have to work hard as long as you live to produce things from the ground to eat.
target_text: ka ama lamatua peka dènge mone ne, èu madhutu boe lii paredha ja'a, te ngaa èu nanene dhoka lii dhèu èmu èu di, ka èu mu'a hua aj'u dhu ja'a kai èèna. nèti èèna ka, èu abhu huku kahèi. aa rai lèke huku kahèi. nèti deo ne'e, toke d'ai èu madhe, hud'i èu kabèli rai, heka èu abhu nganga'a kèna. dènge sab'a bia sèmi ne'e ka, èu heka mamuri kèna.

source_text: thornbushes and thistle plants and other weeds will grow and prevent what you have planted from growing. and for food, you will have to eat things that just grow in your fields.
target_text: masi ka èu sèle rupa-rupa hini èèna ka, te ngaa dhu muri mai dhodhoka dhudhu-sete di.

source_text: all your life you will sweat as you work hard to produce food to eat. then you will die eup, and your body will be buried in the ground. i made you from soil, so when you die and are buried your body will decay and become soil again.
target_text: hud'i èu èi kabhèsu haa ku, heka rai hia èu nganga'a kèna. èu hud'i sab'a bia sèmi èèna ku, toke d'ai lod'o èu madhe. èu ne, ja'a paj'aj'i nèti rai. de ladhe èu madhe, èu j'aj'i hari rai.

source_text: the man, whose name was adam, named his wife eve, which means ‘living', because she became the ancestor of all living people.
target_text: èle èèna ka, adam pangare dhèu èmu na ‘hawa' dhu sasoa na ‘dhu mamuri', te nèngu ka j'aj'i ina nèti dhèu dhu mamuri aa'i-aa'i.

source_text: then yahweh god killed some animals and made clothes from their skins for adam and his wife.
target_text: hèia ama lamatua tao mèdha-papake nèti ka'uri badha, ka papake dua ra.

source_text: then yahweh said, look! those two have become like us because they know what is good to do and what is evil to do. so now, it will not be good if they reach out and pick and eat some of the fruit from the tree which enables people who eat it to live forever!
target_text: ka ama lamatua peka, limuri ne, dhèu re'a le, mia dhu be'a dènge mia dhu karehe, sèmi èdhi kahèi. de mage dhoka, rèngu ra'a hua aj'u dhu èci hari na, dhu hia mamuri taa-taa.

source_text: so yahweh god expelled the man and his wife from the garden of eden. yahweh god had created adam from the ground, but now he forced him to till that ground so that he could grow food to eat.
target_text: èle èèna ka, na babèga eele si nèti d'ara oka eden èèna, ho lasi asa era leo, sèna ka ra mamuri dènge sab'e oka-tedhe. lula dhèu j'aj'i nèti rai, de mamuri kahèi nèti rai.

source_text: after yahweh expelled them, on the east side of the garden he placed ◄cherubim/creatures with wings► and an angel holding a flaming sword which flashed back and forth. he did that in order to block the entrance to the garden, so that people could not go back to the tree that enables people who eat its fruit to live forever.
target_text: babège nare si, ka lamatua paredha ana pajuu na nèti sorga, dhu dènge èla, ho lasi j'aga oka èèna re ca bèka dhimu. rèngu dènge samala dhu heo ha'a-ha'a, dhu seru la'e-mai. lamatua pua si bèdho eele j'ara la'e sa d'ara, te nèngu d'èi boe dhèu puu rare hua aj'u dhu hia ra mamuri taa-taa èèna.

source_text: adam ◄had sex/slept► with his wife eve, and she became pregnant and gave birth to a son whom she named cain, which sounds like the word that means ‘produce', because, she said, by yahweh's help i have produced a son. some time later she gave birth to another son, and she named him abel.
target_text: hèia adam j'unu dènge dhèu èmu na, hawa. ka bhèni ne dènge babia. hèia nara iisi ana mone ca dhèu. ka na peka, aku nèngu na, ja'a abhu le ana mone ca dhèu, lula ama lamatua soru nare le ja'a. ka na pangare ana ne, kaen dhu sasoa na ‘abhu'.

source_text: after those boys grew up, abel ◄tended/took care of► sheep and goats, and cain became a farmer.
target_text: hèia hawa nara iisi hari ana mone èci. ka na pangare ne habel. dua ra kapai ka, habel j'aj'i dhèu madhenge badha. aa a'a na kaen, sab'a oka-tedhe.

source_text: one day cain harvested some of the crops he had grown and brought them to yahweh as a gift for him,
target_text: ca lod'o, kaen nèti isi rai na cahag'e, ka hia lamatua.

source_text: and abel took from his flock some of the first lambs that had been born and killed them and, as a gift, gave to yahweh the fatty parts, which were the best parts. yahweh was pleased with abel and his offering,
target_text: habel nèti ana-ana uuru kahib'i-kalèbho na. na roro kahib'i-kalèbho se, ka nèti sisi dhu be'a hia lamatua. d'ara ama lamatua karej'e ropa ladhe nèdhi korban nèti habel ne.

source_text: but he was not pleased with cain and his offering. so cain became very angry, and his face looked dejected.
target_text: te ngaa na d'èi boe korban unu kaen. hèia kaen nasa bia, ka rèhu na mare boe.

source_text: yahweh said to cain, ◄you should not be angry! /why are you angry? ► rhq ◄you should not scowl like that! /why do you scowl like that? ► rhq
target_text: ka lamatua lii dènge kaen, aku nèngu na, kaen! nga tao ka èu nasa sèmi èèna, ka rèhu èu mare boe?

source_text: if you had done what was right or, if you do what is right rhq, i would accept your offering. but if you do not do what is right, your desire to sin is ready to attack you like a wild animal that prs crouches outside the doorway, ready to spring on its victim met. your desire to sin wants to control you, but you must ◄control/not obey► it.
target_text: ladhe tatao èu be'a, na ja'a sèmi èu dènge hua iia. de mu pangee uuru ku! ladhe èu tao bhelu, na bhabhelu èèna na'e hari èu, sama sèmi meo neo pacèli maraho. de sèmi èu neo tao bhabhelu, be'a risi core eele ka!

source_text: but one day, cain said to his younger brother abel, let's go for a walk in the fields. so they went together. and when they were in the countryside, suddenly cain attacked abel and killed him.
target_text: ca tèka, kaen gale habel, na peka na, mai lati ngad'o oka, we. ropa dua ra d'ai d'ara oka, kaen kalabhe pamadhe ari na.

source_text: later, even though yahweh knew what cain had done, he said to cain, do you know where abel, your younger brother, is? cain replied, no, i do not know. ◄my job is not to guard my younger brother! /am i supposed to take care of my younger brother? ► rhq
target_text: ka lamatua karèi kaen, aku nèngu na, kaen! ari mu ka mia? hèia kaen dhaa, aku nèngu na, ja'a ke'a boe na ètu mia! èu ngee na, ja'a dhèu kèpe haga na, do?

source_text: yahweh said, you have done a terrible thing rhq! so now it is as though your younger brother's voice is crying to me from the ground, demanding that his death must be avenged.
target_text: ka lamatua b'ala, nga tao ka èu bhelu sèmi èèna? baku pangee na, èu pahuni more le raa ari èu ètu d'ara rai, te ja'a dhu kèdhi aa'i-aa'i le!

source_text: you have killed your younger brother, and the ground has soaked up his blood. so now i will expel you from this land and curse your efforts to produce crops.
target_text: de lii dhoo lèke le mi dedha èu. lod'o èu pamadhe ari èu, rai sakid'o nare raa na. de limuri ne, rai bisa heka nèti mamuri mi èu.

source_text: you will till the ground to plant crops, but the ground will produce very few hyp crops. and you will continually wander around the earth, and not have any place to live permanently.
target_text: de ladhe èu sab'a oka-tedhe, rai ne hia heka èu ngaa-ngaa. nèti deo ne'e, èu lu'u sa haa-sa dhimu, sèmi dhèu dhu dènge boe era paleo-palu'u.

source_text: cain replied, you are punishing me more then i can endure.
target_text: te ngaa kaen b'ala lamatua, aku nèngu na, haii! ama lamatua, ee! lamatua dhoo ja'a bia titu kèna, de ja'a pasae mèke boe nga.

source_text: you are about to expel me from the ground that i have been cultivating, and i will no longer be able to come ◄into your presence/and talk with you►. furthermore, i will be continually wandering around the earth with no place to live permanently, and anyone who sees me will kill me.
target_text: lula lamatua bège eele ja'a nèti era ne'e, ja'a kaj'èu nèti ama lamatua. ja'a kako lole-laa asa mia-mia. de ladhe paraga dènge dhèu, èèna na ra pamadhe ja'a.

source_text: but yahweh said to him, no, that will not happen. i will put a mark on you to warn anyone who sees you that i will punish him severely if he kills you. i will punish that person seven times as severely as i am punishing you. then yahweh put a mark on cain's forehead.
target_text: te ngaa lamatua dhaa na, aad'o sèmi èèna! dhèu cee dhu pamadhe èu, èèna na ja'a huku ne, babia na pidhu hari risi nèti èu. hèia lamatua tao tadha mi kaen, sèna ka dhèu re'a ho baku pamadhe ne.

source_text: so cain left yahweh and went to live in the land called nod, which means ‘wandering', which was east of eden.
target_text: hèia kaen tèke eele dènge era èèna. la'e pakaj'èu nèti lamatua, asa era èci, ètu bèka dhimu oka eden. era ne'e, ngara na nod dhu sasoa na, ‘lole-laa'. ka na pea ètu era èèna.

source_text: some time later, cain ◄had sex/slept► with his wife, and she became pregnant and gave birth to a son, whom she named enoch. then cain started to build a city, and he named the city ‘enoch', the same name that his son had.
target_text: hèia kaen leo-èmu, ka dhèu èmu na dènge babia. ka nara iisi ana mone ca dhèu, dhu pangare na henok. hèia kaen patitu rae cue, ngara na henok, madhutu ngara ana na.

source_text: enoch grew up and married and became the father of a son whom he named irad. when irad grew up he became the father of a son whom he named mehujael. mehujael grew up and became the father of a son whom he named methuselah. methuselah grew up and became the father of lamech.
target_text: ka henok matana irad. hèia irad matana mehuyael. mehuyael matana metusael. aa ana metusael, lamek.

source_text: when lamech grew up he married two women. the name of one was adah and the other was zillah.
target_text: dhèu èmu lamek, dhèu dua. èci ngara na ada, aa ca dhèu hari, ngara na sila.

source_text: adah gave birth to a son she named jabal.
target_text: ana ada, ngara na yabal. ana-èpu na, j'aj'i dhèu piara badha. mamuri ra ètu boe ca era, aa ra pea dhoka ètu d'ara paleo di.

source_text: later, jabal was the first person who lived in tents because he traveled from place to place to take care of livestock. his younger brother's name was jubal. he was the first person who made/played a ◄lyre/stringed instrument► and a flute.
target_text: ari yabal, ngara na yubal. ana-èpu yubal, j'aj'i dhèu gai sasadhu, dènge tiu sakino.

source_text: lamech's other wife zillah gave birth to a son whom she named tubal-cain. later tubal-cain became a ◄blacksmith/one who made tools from bronze and iron►. tubal-cain had a younger sister whose name was naamah.
target_text: dhèu èmu lamek èci hari, sila, nara iisi tubal kaen. ana-èpu na j'aj'i tuka bèsi, ka ra tuku mèdha ae-ae tao nèti bèsi, dènge tabaga. ana hèni tubal kaen, ngara na na'ama.

source_text: one day lamech said to his two wives, adah and zillah, listen carefully to what i am saying. a young man struck me and wounded me, so i killed him.
target_text: ca tèka, lamek padedha iisi na ètu madha dhèu èmu dua ra, peka na, mi nanene, ee! deo na, ana mone ngèru èci neo game ja'a. te ngaa ja'a dhadhedhe ne, toke madhe.

source_text: yahweh said long ago that he would avenge and punish anyone who killed cain seven times as much as he punished cain for killing his younger brother. so if anyone tries to kill me, i will punish him 77 times as much as yahweh punished cain.
target_text: dhèu dhu pamadhe kaen, abhu huku pidhu hari. te ngaa cee ka dhu neo b'ala ho pamadhe ja'a, abhu huku pidhu nguru pidhu hari.

source_text: adam continued to ◄have sex/sleep► with eup his wife, and she became pregnant and gave birth to another son, whom she named seth, which sounds like the hebrew word that means ‘given', because, she said, god has given me another child to take the place of abel, since cain killed him.
target_text: ka hawa nara iisi hari ana mone ca dhèu. hèia ra pangare ne, set dhu sasoa na, ‘hia', lula aku hawa na, ama lamatua hia ja'a ana ne, sèna ka gati madha habel, dhu kaen pamadhe ne.

source_text: when seth grew up, he became the father of a son whom he named enosh. about that time people began to worship yahweh again.
target_text: pe d'ai nèbhu ku, set abhu ana mone ca dhèu, dhu pangare na enos. tèu èèna, dhèu mulai manèngi-mangaj'i mi ama lamatua.

source_text: here is a list of the descendants of adam. when god created humans, he caused them to be like him in many ways. he created one man and one woman. he blessed them, and on the day that he created them, he called them ‘human beings'.
target_text: lod'o ama lamatua paj'aj'i dhèu rai-haha, na tao si sama sèmi rupa nèngu. na paj'aj'i si, dhèu mone dènge dhèu bhèni. ka na pangare si ‘dhèu rai-haha', aa na hia si berkat. dhèu dhu uru, ngara na adam. ana-èpu adam, nuka sèmi ne'e ka:

source_text: when adam was 130 years old, he became the father of a son who grew up to be just like him. that was the son he named seth.
target_text: lod'o adam d'ai ca ngasu tèlu nguru tèu, na matana ana mone ca dhèu, dhu rèhu na nare adam. ka pangare na, set.

source_text: after seth was born, adam lived 800 more years, and during those years he became the father of other sons and daughters.
target_text: ka adam mamuri hari d'ai aru ngasu tèu, hèia na abhu hari ana mone dènge ana bhèni.

source_text: adam lived 930 years altogether, and then he died.
target_text: umur adam ceo ngasu tèlu nguru tèu, heka madhe kèna.

source_text: when seth was 105 years old, he became the father of enosh.
target_text: lod'o set d'ai ca ngasu lèmi tèu, na abhu ana mone ca dhèu, ngara na enos.

source_text: after enosh was born, seth lived 807 more years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.
target_text: ka set mamuri hari d'ai aru ngasu pidhu tèu, na abhu hari ana mone dènge ana bhèni.

source_text: seth lived 912 years altogether, and then he died.
target_text: umur set ceo ngasu canguru dua tèu, heka madhe kèna.

source_text: when enosh was 90 years old, he became the father of kenan.
target_text: lod'o enos mamuri d'ai ceo nguru tèu, na matana ana mone ca dhèu, ngara na kenan.

source_text: after kenan was born, enosh lived 815 more years and became the father of other sons and daughters.
target_text: ka enos mamuri hari d'ai aru ngasu canguru lèmi tèu, na abhu hari ana mone dènge ana bhèni.

source_text: enosh lived 905 years altogether, and then he died.
target_text: umur enos ceo ngasu lèmi tèu, heka madhe kèna.

source_text: when kenan was 70 years old, he became the father of mahalalel.
target_text: lod'o kenan d'ai pidhu nguru tèu, na matana ana mone ca dhèu, ngara na mahalalel.

source_text: after mahalalel was born, kenan lived 840 more years and became the father of other sons and daughters.
target_text: ka kenan mamuri hari d'ai aru ngasu èpa nguru tèu, ka na abhu hari ana mone dènge ana bhèni.

source_text: kenan lived 910 years altogether, and then he died.
target_text: umur kenan ceo ngasu canguru tèu, heka madhe kèna.

source_text: when mahalalel was 65 years old, he became the father of jared.
target_text: lod'o mahalalel d'ai èna nguru lèmi tèu, na abhu ana mone ca dhèu, ngara na yared.

source_text: after jared was born, mahalalel lived 830 more years and became the father of other sons and daughters.
target_text: ka mahalalel mamuri hari d'ai aru ngasu tèlu nguru tèu, na abhu hari ana mone dènge ana bhèni.

source_text: mahalalel lived 895 years altogether, and then he died.
target_text: umur mahalalel aru ngasu ceo nguru lèmi tèu, heka na madhe kèna.

source_text: when jared was 162 years old, he became the father of enoch.
target_text: lod'o yared d'ai cangasu èna nguru dua tèu, na abhu ana mone ca dhèu, ngara na henok.

source_text: jared lived 800 years after enoch was born, and he became the father of other sons and daughters.
target_text: ka yared mamuri d'ai aru ngasu tèu, na abhu hari ana mone dènge ana bhèni.

source_text: jared lived 962 years altogether, and then he died.
target_text: umur yared ceo ngasu èna nguru dua tèu, heka madhe kèna.

source_text: when enoch was 65 years old, he became the father of methuselah.
target_text: ropa henok mamuri d'ai èna nguru lèmi tèu, na matana ana mone ca dhèu, ngara na metusalak.

source_text: enoch lived in close fellowship with god for 300 years after methuselah was born, and he became the father of other sons and daughters.
target_text: ele èèna, henok mamuri d'ara èci dènge ama lamatua d'ai tèlu ngasu tèu. ka na abhu hari ana mone dènge ana bhèni.

source_text: enoch lived 365 years altogether in close fellowship with god. then one day he disappeared, because god took him away to be with him in heaven.
target_text: na mamuri d'ara èci dènge ama lamatua. hèia lod'o na d'ai tèlu ngasu èna nguru lèmi tèu, ka na ele, lula ama lamatua paca'e ne sa dedha.

source_text: when methuselah was 187 years old, he became the father of lamech.
target_text: lod'o metusalak d'ai cangasu aru nguru pidhu tèu, na matana ana mone èci, ngara na lamek.

source_text: methuselah lived 782 years after lamech was born, and became the father of other sons and daughters.
target_text: èle èèna ka, metusalak mamuri hari d'ai pidhu ngasu aru nguru dua tèu, ka na abhu hari ana mone dènge ana bhèni.

source_text: methuselah lived 969 years altogether, and then he died.
target_text: umur metusalak ceo ngasu èna nguru ceo tèu, heka madhe kèna.

source_text: when lamech was 182 years old, he became the father of a son,
target_text: lod'o lamek mamuri d'ai ca ngasu aru nguru dua tèu, na matana ana mone ca dhèu.

source_text: whom he named noah, which sounds like the hebrew word that means ‘relief', because he said, he will bring us relief from all the hard work we have been doing to produce food from the ground that yahweh cursed.
target_text: lamek pangare ne noh dhu sasoa na ‘pakarej'e d'ara', lula na peka na, ana ne, èèna na pakarej'e d'ara èdhi nèti sasab'a dhu bia, ètu rai dhu ama lamatua dhoo le.

source_text: lamech lived 595 years after noah was born and became the father of other sons and daughters.
target_text: ka lamek mamuri taruu d'ai lèmi ngasu ceo nguru lèmi tèu, aa na abhu hari ana mone dènge ana bhèni.

source_text: lamech lived 777 years altogether, and then he died.
target_text: umur lamek pidhu ngasu pidhu nguru pidhu tèu, heka na madhe kèna.

source_text: when noah was 500 years old, he became the father of a son whom he named shem. later he became the father of another son whom he named ham, and later he became the father of another son whom he named japheth.
target_text: lod'o noh mamuri d'ai lèmi ngasu tèu, na matana ana mone dhèu tèlu, sem, yafet dènge ham.

source_text: when people began to become very numerous all over the earth, and many daughters were born to them,
target_text: taa èèna, dhèu rai-haha, asa bèba-kacanga. ka ra papala-palème rai-haha. dhèu se matana kahèi ana-ana bhèni.

source_text: some of the men who ◄belonged to/believed in► god saw that some of the women who did not ◄belong to/believe in► god were very beautiful. so they took whichever ones they chose to become their wives.
target_text: ana-ana mone nèti lamatua ladhe rèdhi ana bhèni nèti dhèu rai-haha se, bhèni iia hua. ka lasi todhe rare ana bhèni mia dhu ra d'èi.

source_text: then yahweh said, i will not allow my spirit to keep people alive forever or, the breath of life will not remain in people forever. they will die eventually. they will live not more than 120 years before they die or, there will be only 120 more years before they die.
target_text: ka lamatua peka na, ja'a roca le dènge tatao dhèu dhu lèke-lèke boe se. roh ja'a dhu pamamuri rèngu sa, d'èi heka hia ra mamuri manèro. hud'i rèngu madhe ku. de èèna na, mamuri rèngu se dhoka d'ai ca ngasu dua nguru tèu di.

source_text: there were giants called nephils who lived on the earth at that time and later. during that time some of the nephil men who ◄belonged to/believed in► god had sex eup with women who did not ◄belong to/believe in► god, and they gave birth to children. the nephils were considered to be heroic fighters, and they became famous.
target_text: taa èèna, dènge taa-tebho dhu limuri nèti èèna hari, abhu le dhèu raksasa ètu rai-haha ne. ropa ana mone nèti lamatua leo rare ana bhèni dhèu rai-haha se, ka rara iisi dhèu kapai, nuka: kapala musu, dhèu re'a madhutu lii lolo uru-uru sèra.

source_text: yahweh saw that people on the earth had become very wicked, and that everything they thought about evil things continually.
