source_text: when it was time to harvest wheat, reuben went out into the fields and saw some ◄mandrakes/plants that women eat to help them to become pregnant►. he brought some of them to his mother leah. but rachel saw them and said to leah, please give me some of those plants that your son brought to you!
target_text: ca lod'o, lèke dènge hèru puu-g'ètu are, ruben la'e asa d'ara j'ami. na rage ana aaj'u ca kapua dhu j'aj'i sèmi èi na'i ho hia dhèu bhèni abhu kolo. ka ruben nèti hia ina na lea. ropa rahel nèdhi, ka na peka dènge lea, aku nèngu na, a'a! bagi ku ja'a ciki, èi na'i dhu ruben nèti èèna.

source_text: but leah said to her, no! ◄it was bad that you stole my husband! /is it not bad enough that you stole my husband? ► rhq now ◄are you going to take my son's mandrake plants? /you want to take my son's mandrake plants also, so that you can become pregnant! ► rhq so rachel said, all right, jacob can sleep with you tonight, if you give me some of your son's mandrake plants. so leah ◄agreed/gave her some►.
target_text: te ngaa lea b'ala, aku nèngu na, wee! èu ne seli-kolane! parame more le dhèu èmu ja'a. te ngaa roca mèka na. mu neo hari unu aj'u èi na'i èèna nèti ana ja'a? me'a heka makae d'ara! te ngaa rahel dhaa, sèmi ne'e, a'a! ladhe ja'a abhu èi na'i na, mèda ne'e èu pa'èci dènge yakob. ka lea d'èi kahèi.

source_text: when jacob returned from the wheat fields that evening, leah went out to meet him. she said, you must sleep with me tonight, because i gave rachel some of my son's mandrakes that enable women to become pregnant, to pay her for allowing us to do that. so jacob slept with her that night.
target_text: ka pe d'ai loo nihia sa, yakob lèpa nèti d'ara oka. lea la'e soru nare ne, ka na peka, a'a! mèda ne, èu j'unu dènge ja'a! lula ja'a dhu hèli kore le èu, dènge kab'ua èi na'i ana ja'a! ka mèda na, yakob j'unu dènge lea.

source_text: god answered leah's prayers, and she became pregnant and bore a fifth son to jacob.
target_text: ka ama lamatua tadèngi lii manèngi-mangaj'i lea. nèti èèna ka, na dènge babia, hèia nara iisi ana mone ka lèmi.

source_text: leah said, god has rewarded me for giving my slave to my husband to be another wife for him. so she named him issachar, which sounds like the hebrew word that means ‘reward'.
target_text: hèia lea pangare ana na, isaskar, dhu sasoa na, ‘b'ae j'aj'èra', lula na peka na, ama lamatua b'ae-baj'a le j'aj'èra ja'a, lula ja'a hia le silpa madhèdi dènge dhèu èmu ja'a.

source_text: leah became pregnant again and bore a sixth son for jacob.
target_text: èle èèna ka, lea dènge babia hari, hèia nara iisi ana mone ka èna.

source_text: leah said, god has given me a precious gift. ◄this time/now► my husband will honor/respect me, because i have given birth to six sons for him. so she named him zebulon, which sounds like the hebrew word that means ‘accepted gift'.
target_text: ka na peka, aku nèngu na, ama lamatua parasee ja'a mèdha dhu be'a. ka limuri ne, dhèu èmu ja'a hud'i pakab'ua ku ja'a, lula ja'a matana hia ne ana mone dhèu èna. nèti èèna ka, na pangare ana ne, sebulon dhu sasoa na ‘pakab'ua'.

source_text: later she gave birth to a daughter, and named her dinah.
target_text: ka lea nara iisi hari, te ngaa ana bhèni, ka na pangare na, dina.

source_text: then god thought about what rachel wanted. he heard her prayers and enabled her to become pregnant.
target_text: te ngaa ama lamatua dhu bhèlu boe rahel, ka sèmi lii manèngi-mangaj'i na. nèti èèna ka, na bhoke era ana na.

source_text: she became pregnant and gave birth to a son. she said, god has caused that no longer will i be ashamed for not having children.
target_text: hèia rahel dènge babia, ka nara iisi ana mone ca dhèu. ka na peka, ama lamatua saku eele le d'ara makae ja'a.

source_text: she named him joseph, which sounds like the hebrew words that mean ‘may he give another' and she said, ‘ want yahweh to give me another son. '
target_text: hèia na pangare ana na yusuf dhu sasoa na ele boe ‘hud'i laa na hia tabha hari', lula aku nèngu na, ja'a manèngi, sèna ka ama lamatua hia ja'a ana mone ca dhèu hari.

source_text: after rachel had given birth to joseph, jacob said to laban, now allow me to quit working for you and let me return to my own land.
target_text: lod'o rahel nara iisi yusuf, yakob peka dènge laban, aku nèngu na, to'o! ladhe mo'o, ja'a neo lèpa asa rai ètu-èsu ja'a.

source_text: you know the work that i have done for you for a long time to get my wives. so let me take my wives and my children, and leave.
target_text: ja'a neo laku dènge ana-dhèu èmu ja'a. to'o, èu dhu me'a le, ja'a ne sab'a tèu-tèu nèti mad'ae d'ai loo nihia. de ja'a b'ae pama'ète le rèngu se. nèti èèna ka, rèngu se, j'aj'i le unu ja'a ka teme aae.

source_text: but laban said to him, if you are pleased with me, stay here, because i have found out by performing a magic ritual that yahweh has blessed me because of what you have done for me.
target_text: hèia, aku to'o na, ana, ee! èu nanene ku lii ja'a laa! madhutu lii malare dhu ja'a abhu, lamatua hia ja'a mamèngi lula èu.

source_text: tell me what you want me to pay you for continuing to work for me, and that is what i will pay you.
target_text: de èu neo manèngi ca ngaa, peka, sèna ka ja'a b'ae! sad'i èu baku tèke eele ja'a, te ngaa sab'a taruu hia ja'a.

source_text: jacob replied, you know how i have worked for you, and you know that your livestock have increased greatly as i have taken care of them.
target_text: ka yakob peka, to'o! èu mèdhi unu mu le, sasab'a-la'a ja'a. nèti èèna ka, badha-manu to'o se, bèba-kacanga.

source_text: you had only a few animals before i came here. but now you have very many, and yahweh has caused them to increase greatly in number wherever i have taken them. but now i need to start taking care of the needs of my own family.
target_text: lod'o dhu ja'a dhae mai mèka, mèdha-panyau to'o ku ae èèna mèka. te ngaa limuri ne, to'o kaja le. lamatua pala-bagi le to'o ku mamèngi, lula sasab'a-la'a ja'a ka. te d'ai le lod'o na, sèna ka ja'a sab'a hia ana-dhèu èmu ja'a.

source_text: laban replied, what do you want me to give you? jacob replied, i do not want you to pay me anything. but if you will do this one thing for me, i will continue to take care of your flocks and protect them.
target_text: hèia laban karèi ne, aku nèngu na, de sèmi èèna na, ja'a b'ae èu tasamia? ka yakob dhaa, peka na, to'o ku, hia ia ka ja'a ngaa-ngaa. te ngaa badha-manu to'o ku, ja'a ladhe-leru taruu, sad'i mu tao ku j'ara èci.

source_text: allow me to go and look at all of your flocks today and remove from them all the speckled sheep, all the spotted sheep, and every dark-colored lamb, all the goats that are speckled, and all the goats that are spotted, and keep them for myself. they will be my wages.
target_text: ladhe mo'o, deo ne'e kahèi, ja'a laku asa badha-manu to'o sèi, ho hag'e si. mia dhu dènge boe katèd'a aa dènge boe karata, sèra sa unu to'o ku taruu. te ngaa mia dhu dènge katèd'a aa dhu karata, hia mi ja'a. dènge kahib'i-kalèbho dhu mèdhi, ja'a kora aa'i si. se'e se, hud'i laa j'aj'i mi bab'ae rui-j'aj'èra ja'a.

source_text: in that way, in the future, you will be able to know whether i have been honest regarding what you have paid me. if any of my goats are neither speckled or spotted, or if any of my lambs are not dark-colored, you will know that i have stolen them from you.
target_text: d'ai lod'o limuri, pe to'o me'a ja'a ne sab'a dènge mola, do aad'o. sad'i lake more, mai ho mu parisa badha-manu ja'a. ladhe mu abhu kahib'i-ka'ia dhu dènge boe katèd'a, aa dhu karata boe, do, kahib'i-kalèbho dhu pudhi, èèna na, dhu me'a le èèna, ja'a mana'u badha-manu to'o.

source_text: laban agreed and said, okay, we will do as you have said.
target_text: ka laban d'èi kahèi, aku nèngu na, oo! j'ara na sèmi èèna ka.

source_text: but that same day laban removed all the male goats that had black and white stripes on them or were spotted, and all the female goats that were speckled or spotted, all the goats that were partly white, and all the dark-colored lambs. he separated them and told his sons to take care of them.
target_text: te ngaa ètu d'ara lod'o èèna kahèi, laban hag'e dènge badha dhu katèd'a, dhu karata, dènge kahib'i-kalèbho dhu mèdhi. ka na pangèd'u mi ana na si, ho ladhe-leru.

source_text: then he took these flocks and walked a distance of three days, in order that he could be that far from jacob. jacob continued to take care of the rest of laban's flocks.
target_text: hèia eo rèti ka badha se asa era èci dhu kaj'èu na tèlu lod'o kako haga nèti era yakob si. ka yakob madhenge ka badha dhu ata se.

source_text: then jacob cut some branches of ◄poplar, almond, and plane trees/three kinds of trees that had white wood►. he peeled strips of bark from the branches, so that where the bark had been peeled off, the branches were light in color.
target_text: èla èèna ka, yakob poro nare dadana aaj'u nèti aj'u tèlu rupa. ka na caci pakarata ka'uri aj'u sèra, tao strep-strep.

source_text: then he placed the peeled branches in the troughs where they put the water for the animals to drink, so that the branches would be in front of the flocks when they came to drink.
target_text: hèia aj'u dhu strep-strep se, na tèke asa d'ara karab'a kahib'i. badha se dhu tema le pa'ango aa paleo ètu era èèna.

source_text: the animals also mated in front of the branches, and eventually they gave birth to animals that were speckled, or to animals that were spotted, or to animals that had black and white stripes on them.
target_text: de ladhe badha se paleo ètu madha aj'u strep-strep se, ra matana ana dhu rèu ra katèd'a dènge karata.

source_text: furthermore, jacob separated the female sheep in his flock from the other sheep and goats in laban's flock. and when his female sheep mated, he made them look toward the animals that belonged to laban that had black and white stripes on them, and the dark-colored animals. he did that so that the female sheep would give birth to animals that were striped or dark-colored. by doing that, he made bigger flocks for himself, and he kept them separate from laban's flocks.
target_text: ka ladhe badha laban se neo paleo, yakob patangare si asa kahib'i dhu katèd'a dènge karata sèra. hèia ana dhu ra matana sa rèu ra katèd'a dènge karata kahèi. dènge j'ara sèmi èèna ka, badha na asa ae. ka na pacèri eele si nèti badha laban sèra.

source_text: in addition, whenever the stronger female sheep were ready to mate, jacob put some of those peeled branches in the troughs in front of them, so that they would mate in front of the branches.
target_text: ropa badha dhu èra neo paleo, yakob nare kadhèli aj'u dhu strep-strep sèra, tao mi d'ara karab'a ètu madha si.

source_text: but when weak animals were ready to mate, he did not put the branches in their troughs. so the weak ones became part of laban's flock, and the strong ones became part of jacob's flock.
target_text: te ngaa ladhe kahib'i dhu roe dènge malaka-god'a neo paleo, yakob soro tèke si. ka badha dhu roe, sèra unu to'o na laban. aa mia dhu èra, sèra unu nèngu.

source_text: as a result, jacob became very rich. he owned many large flocks of sheep and goats, and many male and female slaves, and many camels and donkeys.
target_text: dènge j'ara ne'e ne, yakob j'aj'i dhèu kaja-su'i. ka kahib'i-ka'ia na, kahib'i-kalèbho na, onta na, keled'ei na, dènge ènu na bhèni-mone, udhu sobhu-sobhu.

source_text: someone told jacob that laban's sons were complaining and saying, jacob has become very rich by taking everything hyp that belonged to our father.
target_text: ca tèka, yakob tadèngi lii padhai ana-ana laban se, aku rèngu na, kakaja-sasu'i yakob sèra, lula na kao nare aa'i mèdha-panyau ama èdhi.

source_text: and jacob noticed that laban was not acting friendly toward him as he had done before.
target_text: yakob nèdhi kahèi rèhu to'o laban mare heka, aa be'a heka dènge ne, sèmi uru èèna.

source_text: then yahweh said to jacob, go back to your country and your relatives, and i will help you there.
target_text: hèia lamatua peka dènge yakob, d'ai le lod'o, ho èu lèpa asa ina dènge ama mu. ja'a palere-lere dènge èu.

source_text: so jacob sent a message to rachel and leah, telling them to come out to the pastures where his flocks of sheep and goats were.
target_text: ka yakob hia dhèu lasi paroa rahel dènge lea, sèna ka mai paraga dènge ne ètu era ani badha, ètu d'ara mamoo.

source_text: when they arrived, he said to them, i see that your father does not act friendly toward me as he did previously. but god, whom my father worshiped, has helped me.
target_text: hèia na peka dènge ra, aku nèngu na, limuri ne, ja'a ladhe-ladhe na, ama miu na rèhu na mare heka dènge ja'a. aa babe'a na mi ja'a, sèmi heka uru èèna. te ngaa ama lamatua dhu ama ku sogo-tagu èèna, palere-lere dènge ja'a.

source_text: you two know that i have worked very hard for your father,
target_text: miu dua mi se me'a le, nèbhu nare sange ne'e, ja'a j'aj'i kuli ètu ama miu!

source_text: but many times hyp he has cheated me by decreasing my wages. but god has not allowed him to harm me.
target_text: te ngaa sèmi èèna, d'ara na la'e kahèi, ka na kapod'e-kabèli taruu ja'a. ka na ub'a rui-j'aj'èra ja'a, canguru hari kèna. masi ka sèmi èèna, ama lamatua j'aga pa'èra ja'a.

source_text: when laban said, ‘the speckled animals are the ones that i will give you to be your wages, ' then all the animals gave birth to young ones that were speckled. when he changed and said, ‘the ones that have black and white stripes on them will be your wages, ' then all the animals gave birth to young ones that were striped.
target_text: lod'o ama miu peka na, ‘badha dhu rèu ra katèd'a sèra j'aj'i mi unu èu, ' ho ladhe lod'o badha se matana, ana dhu katèd'a hua-hua. lod'o leo hari, na peka, ‘badha dhu karata sèra, j'aj'i mi unu èu, ' ka badha se matana ana karata aa'i-aa'i.

source_text: in that way, god has taken away the livestock that belonged to your father and has given them to me.
target_text: ama lamatua ad'u sèmi èèna na, sèna ka nare aa'i badha-manu ama miu èèna, ho hia mi ja'a.

source_text: one time, when the animals were mating, i had a dream. in my dream i looked up and was surprised to see that some of the male goats that were mating with the female goats had black and white stripes on them, some were speckled, and some were spotted.
target_text: ca tèka, ropa badha se paleo, ja'a kèdhi ètu d'ara nii, dhu peka na, badha mone aa'i-aa'i dhu paleo, abhu dhu katèd'a aa dhu karata hèi.

source_text: an angel who was sent by god said to me in the dream, ‘jacob! ' i replied, ‘i am here! '
target_text: ka ana pajuu lamatua nèti sorga paroa ja'a, peka na, ‘yakob! ' hèia ja'a dhaa, ‘tasamia, lamatua? '

source_text: he said to me, ‘look up and you will see that all the male goats that are mating have black and white stripes on them, or are speckled or spotted. this is happening because i have seen all that laban has done to you.
target_text: ka na lii, ‘ladhe ku laa! badha mone dhu paleo sèra, dhodhoka dhu karata dènge katèd'a di. ja'a ka ad'u sèra sa, lula ja'a dhu kèdhi le, ngaa dhu laban tao mi dedha èu.

source_text: i am god who appeared to you at bethel, where you set up a stone to show that the place was holy, and you poured olive oil on the stone and made a solemn promise to me. so now leave this land immediately, and return to the land where you were born. '
target_text: ja'a ne, ama lamatua, dhu pad'elo iisi mi èu ètu betel èèna. ètu era nèi, èu patitu hadhu, ka mu bhori èi mènyi ètu dedha na, ka èu sogo-tagu ja'a. ka èu pa'èki lii pajaji dènge ja'a ètu nèi. de kèd'i ka, tèke eele ka rai ne'e ne, lamu ka asa kabarai ina-ama èu. '

source_text: rachel and leah replied, our father will not give us anything more when he dies rhq.
target_text: hèia rahel dènge lea b'ala lii na, aku rèngu na, la'a ma! ji'i dènge heka pusaka ngaa-ngaa nèti ama ji'i laban.

source_text: he treats us as though we were foreigners rhq! your working for him all these years was like a payment that you gave him as a price for us, but we will not inherit any of that money that he got as a price for us. he has spent it all!
target_text: nèbhu nare sange ne'e, mone heka ne tao ji'i sèmi dhèu leo kara sa. na pahie eele le ji'i se. ka na'e aa'i le kab'ua-kadheli ji'i se.

source_text: surely all of the wealth that god took away from our father belongs to us and to our children. so do whatever god has told you to do!
target_text: de mèdha-panyau dhu ama lamatua nare sèra nèti ama ji'i laban, aa'i-aa'i sèra j'aj'i le unu èdhi dènge ana-ana èdhi se. de ladhe aku lamatua tasa mera mia, te'a dhoka madhutu di!

source_text: then jacob put his children and his wives on camels. he made all his livestock go ahead of him. besides the livestock, he took along all the other things that he had acquired while living in paddan-aram. and they prepared to return to his father isaac, in the canaan region.
target_text: èle èèna ka, yakob lalau mèdha-panyau na. hèia na paca'e ana-dhèu èmu na asa dedha onta lasi, aa na eo nèti badha-manu na aa'i-aa'i, dènge mèdha-panyau dhu na abhu ètu padan aram, ho lasi asa rai kana'an.

source_text: before they left, while laban was shearing his sheep, rachel stole the small wooden idols that were in her father's tent.
target_text: lod'o èèna, laban dhu la'e g'ute rèu kahib'i-kalèbho na. ka rahel mana'u nare patung mèdha sogo-tagu ama na.

source_text: furthermore, jacob deceived laban, who belonged to the aram people-group, by not telling him that they were planning to leave.
target_text: aa yakob si lasi palangu boe lii dènge to'o na.

source_text: so jacob and his family fled with all their possessions, and they crossed the euphrates river, and then started traveling south toward the hilly gilead region.
target_text: na bau nèti aa'i mèdha-panyau na, ka ra kako pamèri-mèri, lasi re loko efrat, asa ledhe gilead.

source_text: on the third day after they left, someone told laban that jacob and his family had left.
target_text: rarai yakob si èèna d'ai tèlu lod'o ku, heka laban ne'a kèna.

source_text: so he took some of his relatives with him and started to pursue jacob. they continued walking for seven days.
target_text: hèia laban oru nare ka dhèu-dhèu na, lasi bate yakob si. d'ai pidhu lod'o ku, heka ra paraga dènge si ètu ledhe gilead.

source_text: then god appeared to laban in a dream at night, and said to him, when you catch up to jacob, be sure that you do not say anything at all hyp to him in an angry manner!
target_text: ka d'ara mèda èèna, lamatua pad'elo iisi na mi laban ètu d'ara nii. na peka na, laban! ladhe èu padhai lii dènge yakob, j'aga paie hèb'a èu na.

source_text: the next day, by the time laban caught up with jacob, jacob and his household had set up their tents in the hilly gilead region. so laban and his relatives set up their tents there, too.
target_text: mèda èèna, yakob si dhu patitu paleo ètu ledhe gilead. aa laban si patitu unu ra kaj'èu boe nèti era èèna kahèi.

source_text: then laban went to jacob and said to him, why have you done this? you have deceived me by carrying away my daughters as though you had captured them in a war mty!
target_text: èle ka, laban mai paraga dènge yakob. hèia na lii, aku nèngu na, nga tao ka, èu rai mèti ana bhèni ja'a se, dènge boe lii ugu-ge'e sa hèi? mu tao si sèmi dhèu dhu èu segi ètu d'ara papara-pakèj'i.

source_text: why did you run away and deceive me? why did you not tell me that you were going to leave, so that we could have rejoiced and sung while people played music on tambourines and harps before i said ‘goodbye' to you?
target_text: èu ne ad'a aad'o, palangu boe sa hèi dènge ja'a! ladhe èu peka dènge ja'a be'a-be'a, ele boe ja'a tao sisi-kau, ho ta'a-tinu boko-boko, ho lere miu dènge lii sod'a, heka ji'i patabuli miu kèna.

source_text: ◄you did not even let me kiss my grandchildren and my daughters goodbye before they left! /why did you not allow me to kiss my grandchildren and daughters goodbye before they left? ► rhq what you have done was foolish!
target_text: sasala èu èci hari ka, èu hia boe ja'a uu ana-èpu ja'a hèi. tatao èu ne goa titu kèna!

source_text: my relatives and i have the power to harm you, but last night the god whom your father worships said to me in a dream, ‘be sure that you do not say anything at all to jacob in an angry way. '
target_text: carui boe, ladhe ja'a ne neo paj'èra èu! te ngaa malo-malo ka mèda-mèda na, ama lamatua dhu ama mu sogo-tagu èèna, kai ja'a peka na, ladhe ja'a padhai lii dènge èu, ja'a hud'i j'aga paie-iie ku hèb'a ja'a.

source_text: now, i know you have left because you long to go back home. but why did you steal my wooden idols?
target_text: mema, ja'a dhu ke'a le, èu pakèd'i lula èu dhu neo le lèpa. te ngaa tasamia ka, èu mana'u mèti patung mèdha sogo-tagu ja'a?

source_text: jacob replied to laban, saying, i did not tell you that we were planning to leave, because i was afraid. i thought that if i told you, you would forcefully take your daughters away from me.
target_text: hèia yakob b'ala, aku nèngu na, to'o baku nasa ku dènge ja'a! ja'a pakèd'i mau-mau èèna, lula ja'a mage dhoka mo'o boe ja'a kèti ana-ana se!

source_text: but if you find anyone here who has your wooden idols, we will execute that person. while our relatives are watching, search for yourself to see if there is anything that belongs to you that is here with me. if you find anything, you can take it! when jacob said that, he did not know that rachel had stolen the wooden idols.

target_text: ropa esau nèdhi bhèni dènge ana-ana si, ka na karèi, aku nèngu na, se'e se, cee ka se'e? ka yakob peka, rèngu se'e se, dhu ama lamatua pala-bagi hia ja'a, ènu a'a ku ne.

source_text: but esau replied, my younger brother, i have enough animals! keep for yourself the animals that you have!
target_text: te ngaa esau peka, ja'a dènge mèdha-panyau ae kahèi. de hia ia ka ja'a ngaa-ngaa.

source_text: but jacob said, no, please, if you feel good toward me, accept these gifts from me. you have greeted me very kindly. seeing your smiling face assures me that you have forgiven me. it is like seeing the face of god!
target_text: te ngaa yakob b'ala, peka na, baku, a'a. a'a ku hud'i sèmi la mèdha se, sèna ka j'aj'i mi tadha, peka na, a'a ku sèmi ja'a dènge d'ara taleo. te ropa a'a ku b'ui mari, ka ja'a sèmi dhu kèdhi b'ui mari nèti ama lamatua.

source_text: please accept these gifts that i have brought to you, because god has acted kindly toward me, and i still have plenty of animals! jacob kept on urging him to accept the animals, and finally he accepted them.

source_text: then esau said, let's continue traveling together, and i will show the road to you.

target_text: te ngaa aku yakob na, hud'i laa, a'a! a'a ku ladhe mèdhi unu mu. ana mu se, ana iiki ae era. rèngu se dhae èra èèna mèka. aa badha ae ka dhu heka matana. ladhe ta pakaseti si kako pamèri, ètu d'ara ca lod'o, èèna na madhe aa'i si.

source_text: you go ahead of me. i will lead the animals slowly, but i will walk as fast as the children and animals can walk. i will catch up with you in seir, in the land where the descendants of edom live.

source_text: esau said, then allow me to leave with you some of the men who came with me, to protect you. but jacob replied, ◄why do that? /there is no need to do that! ► rhq the only thing that i want is for you to act friendly toward me.
target_text: hèia esau lii hari, na peka, ladhe sèmi èèna, ja'a tèke eele dhèu ja'a se cahag'e, sèna ka pad'elo j'ara hia miu. te ngaa, aku yakob na, hud'i laa, a'a, ee! sad'i ja'a ke'a le, a'a ku sèmi ja'a dènge be'a.

source_text: so on that day esau left to return to seir.
target_text: tadèngi nare, esau pakèd'i ka, tèke eele si, lèpa asa seir.

source_text: but instead of going to seir, jacob and his family went to a place called succoth. there he built a house for himself and his family, and built shelters for his livestock. that is the reason they named the place succoth, which means ‘shelters'.
target_text: te ngaa nèti era èèna, yakob la'e asa sukot. d'ai nèi, na tao èmu dènge oka hia badha aa'i-aa'i ra. nèti èèna ka, era èèna ra pangare na sukot dhu sasoa na ‘èmu pea taha'.

source_text: some time later, jacob and his family left paddan-aram in mesopotamia, and they traveled safely to the canaan region. there they set up their tents in a field near shechem city.
target_text: te ngaa nèbhu boe ka, yakob si kako nèti padan aram, lasi d'ai rae sikem ètu rai kana'an dènge sod'a-mole. hèia ra patitu paleo, sèna ka ra pea padètu dènge rae èèna.

source_text: one of the leaders of the people in that area was named hamor. hamor had several sons. jacob paid the sons of hamor 100 pieces of silver for the piece of ground on which they set up their tents.
target_text: rai dhu yakob patitu paleo ne, hèli nare nèti hemor, ana sikem. kab'ua rai ne, ca ngasu doi iia.

source_text: he built a stone altar there, and named it el-elohe israel, which means ‘god, the god of israel. '

source_text: one day dinah, the daughter of jacob and leah, went to visit some of the women in that area.

source_text: shechem, one of the sons of hamor, the ruler of that area who was descended from the hiv people-group, saw her. he wanted her. so he grabbed her and forced her to have sex eup with him.
target_text: dhèu aae kabarai ne, ngara na hemor, nèti suku hewi. ngara ana mone na, sikem. ca tèka, sikem ladhe nèdhi dina, ka rai nèti ne, hèia na tao pakarehe ne.

target_text: sikem d'èi madhe-madhe dina ne. ka na solo mako, sèna ka dina no'o dènge ne.

source_text: so shechem said to his father hamor, please get this girl for me. i want her to become my wife!
target_text: hèia sikem peka dènge ama na, aku nèngu na, ama! lamu karèi dina hia ja'a, sèna ka ja'a madhèdi dènge ne.

source_text: jacob very soon found out that his daughter dinah had been disgraced/defiled. but his sons were in the fields with his livestock, so he did nothing about it until they returned home.
target_text: tatao sikem ne, yakob dhu tadèngi le, te ngaa na mau-mau, aa tao boe ngaa-ngaa. te lod'o èèna, ana mone na sèra, ètu d'ara pad'a madhenge badha rèngu. ka na mate si mai ku.

source_text: in the meantime, shechem's father hamor went to talk with jacob.
target_text: lod'o èèna, hemor, ama sikem, mai padhai lii dènge yakob, ho neo karèi dina hia sikem.

source_text: while they were still talking, jacob's sons came in from the field. when they found out what had happened, they were shocked and very angry. they said, shechem has done something that is very disgraceful among us israeli people, something that never should be done!
target_text: ètu talora dua ra padhue-padhai era, ana-ana yakob lèpa nèti d'ara pad'a. ropa ra tadèngi sikem dhu tao pakarehe le ana hèni ra, ka d'ara ra pèd'a, ka ra nasa bia. ka ra peka, madha j'ara dhu sèmi ne'e ne, lèke boe ètu isra'el. de ji'i se sèmi boe dhèu tao bhelu-katub'a sèmi èèna.

source_text: but hamor said to them, my son shechem really likes this girl. please allow him to marry her.
target_text: ka hemor pamako yakob, aku nèngu na, ana ja'a sikem d'èi tare'a-re'a ana èu dina. de ja'a manèngi d'ara èu, sèna ka mo'o la, paleo ana bhèni èu dènge ne.

source_text: let's make an agreement: you will give your daughters to our young men to be their wives, and we will give our daughters to your young men to be their wives.
target_text: ladhe mo'o ana-ana èdhi se paleo iisi-aanga ra. ana-ana mone nèti miu, madhèdi dènge ana-ana bhèni nèti ji'i. sèmi èèna kahèi, ana-ana mone ji'i madhèdi dènge ana-ana bhèni miu.

source_text: you can live among us, and live anywhere in our land that you wish. you can buy and sell things or, travel around and if you find land that you want, then you can buy it.
target_text: sèna ka èdhi pea pa'oru pa'èci ètu d'ara rai ne'e. sad'i miu d'èi era mia èèna ka, mi pea la dènge boe ngaa-ngaa. mi d'aga, sèna ka abhu kakaja ètu ne'e.

source_text: then shechem said to dinah's father and brothers, if you feel good toward me and do what i am asking for, i will give you whatever you ask for. tell me what gifts you want and what bride price you want, and i will give you what you ask for. i just want you to give the girl to me to be my wife.
target_text: hèia sikem peka dènge ama dina dènge a'a na sèra, peka na, miu se, sad'i manèngi ngaa, ja'a dhoka madhutu di. masi ka miu manèngi doi pamèu madha, dènge kab'ua pèri-pèri èèna ka, ja'a hia. sad'i mo'o ja'a leo dènge ana hèni miu.

source_text: but because shechem had done a shameful thing to their sister dinah, the sons of jacob deceived shechem and his father hamor
target_text: te ngaa ana-ana yakob se re'a le, sikem dhu tao pakarehe ana hèni ra dina. hèia ra karihu-kahadhu, ka ra bèle, peka mi sikem dènge ama na hemor,

source_text: by saying to them, no, we cannot do that. we cannot give our sister to be the wife of a man who is not circumcised, because that would be a shameful thing for us to do.
target_text: aku rèngu na, ji'i bisa boe hia ana hèni ji'i leo dènge dhèu dhu suna boe. te èèna na, era makae ji'i èèna!

source_text: we will do that only if you do one thing: you must become like us by circumcising all the males that are among you.
target_text: te ngaa j'ara na sèmi ne'e: miu se, hud'i sama ku sèmi ji'i, mone aa'i-aa'i ra, ana iiki, dhèu kapai, hud'i suna ku.

source_text: then we will give our daughters to your young men to be your wives, and we will take your daughters to be the wives of our young men. we will live among you, and we will become one people-group.
target_text: ladhe miu madhutu j'ara ne'e, èdhi heka paleo kèna. aa ji'i pea ètu rai ne'e hèi, sèna ka èdhi j'aj'i mi èci.

source_text: but if you will not agree to being circumcised, we will take our sister and go back to our land.
target_text: te ngaa ladhe miu madhutu boe dad'èi ji'i, aa mo'o boe suna, ji'i ngare hari ana hèni ji'i, ho kèd'i eele rai ne'e.

source_text: what they said pleased hamor and his son shechem.
target_text: hèia hemor dènge ana na sikem ro'o kahèi.

source_text: shechem was very much in love with jacob's daughter, so he quickly agreed to do what they suggested.
target_text: te ngaa sikem no'o heka mate, lula d'ara na d'èi ae dina. dhèu isi rai ètu èèna pakab'ua sikem ne titu kèna.

source_text: shechem went with hamor to the meeting place near the city gate, and they spoke to the city leaders, saying,

source_text: these men are friendly toward us. we should let them live here and travel around or, buy and sell things and if they find land that they want, they can buy it. there is plenty of land for them to live here. our young men can marry their daughters, and their young men can marry our daughters.

source_text: but these men will agree to live among us and become one people-group with us only if all our males are circumcised, as they are.
target_text: lii manèngi rèngu dhoka èci di, nèti èdhi se. ra manèngi, èdhi mone se aa'i-aa'i hud'i suna ku, madhutu ad'a rèngu.

source_text: but if we do that, just think! their livestock and their possessions and their other animals will become ours rhq! so we should agree to do what they suggest, and then they will live among us!
target_text: ladhe èdhi se pab'ali le dènge rèngu, èèna na badha-manu dènge mèdha-panyau ra j'aj'i unu èdhi. de be'a risi èdhi to'o la madhutu dad'èi ra. mai sèna ka aa'i-aa'i ti suna! mo'o, sina ma?

source_text: shechem was the most respected person in his father's household, so all the men who were there at the city gate agreed to what hamor and shechem suggested. so every male in the city was circumcised.
target_text: ka dhèu aa'i-aa'i ètu sèra sa, sèmi lii padhai lii hemor dènge ana na sikem. hèia dhèu mone aa'i-aa'i ètu rai èèna suna palere-lere.

source_text: on the third day after that, when the men of the city were still sore because of being circumcised, two of jacob's sons, simeon and levi, who were dinah's brothers, took their swords and entered the city without anyone opposing them, and killed all the men.
target_text: d'ara lod'o ka tèlu, ropa rèngu dhu suna se, nu'a ra dhu pèd'a era, ka ana mone dina, simeon dènge lewi, rare samala ra, kako mau-mau, lasi asa d'ara kota. ka dua ra pare pamadhe aa'i-aa'i dhèu mone sèra.

source_text: they even killed hamor and his son shechem. then they took dinah out of shechem's house and left the city.
target_text: hemor dènge sikem, ra pare pamadhe kahèi. hèia ra rèti dènge ka dina nèti d'ara èmu sikem, lèpa èmu rèngu.

source_text: then the other sons of jacob went into the city where all those dead bodies were. they ◄looted/took everything in► the city to get revenge for the shameful thing that had been done to their sister.

source_text: then jacob said to simeon and levi, you have caused a lot of trouble for me! now the canaan people-group and the perizzi people-group and everyone else who lives in this land will ◄hate me/say my name stinks►! i do not have many men to fight for us, so if they all gather together and come to me and attack us, they will destroy us and all our household!

source_text: but they replied, ◄should we have allowed shechem to treat our sister like a prostitute? /we could not just let shechem treat our sister like a prostitute! ► rhq
target_text: te ngaa ana se dhaa dènge lii nasa, peka na, ama! ama pangee na hud'i laa ji'i soro tèke si, sèna ka ra tao ana hèni ji'i ne, bhèni kajeo!

source_text: some time later god said to jacob, go up to bethel, and live there. build an altar to worship me, god, who appeared to you when you were fleeing from your older brother esau.
target_text: èle èèna ka, ama lamatua padhai lii dènge yakob, peka na, ja'a ne, ama lamatua dhu pad'elo iisi mi èu, lod'o èu rai nèti madha a'a mu esau. kèd'i, lamu dènge ka asa betel. ladhe d'ai nèi, mu patitu mei korban hia ja'a. aa pea dènge ka ètu èèna.

source_text: so jacob said to his household and to all the others who were with him, get rid of the idols you brought from mesopotamia. also, bathe yourselves and put on clean clothes. then we will get ready and go up to bethel. there i will make an altar to worship god. he is the one who helped me at the time when i was greatly distressed and afraid, and he has been with me wherever i have gone.
target_text: ka yakob peka dènge isi èmu na aa'i-aa'i, aku nèngu na, aa'i-aa'i ti lati dènge ka asa betel. uru èèna, lod'o ja'a ètu d'ara j'aj'èra, ama lamatua ka dhu ladhe-leru ja'a ètu èèna. ja'a neo tao mei korban ètu nèi. de mi core eele mèdha sogo-tagu miu. aa mi pamèu iisi mi, ho mi gati mèdha-papake leo, te èdhi neo pahaha iisi mi ama lamatua.

source_text: jacob and all those who were with him came to luz, which is now called bethel, in the canaan region.
target_text: ka yakob si d'ai dènge sod'a ètu betel dhu uru èèna, ngara na lus, ètu rai kana'an.

source_text: deborah, who had taken care of isaac's wife rebekah when rebekah was a small girl, was now very old. she died and was buried under an oak tree south of bethel. so they named that place allon-bacuth, which means ‘oak of weeping'.
target_text: padètu dènge rae betel, abhu aj'u aae ca kapua, ngara na alon bakut. sasoa na ‘aj'u tangi dhèu madhe'. pake ngara ne, lod'o debora, ina dhu lalau-lalo'o ribka, madhe, ka padhane ètu karasa aj'u èèna.

source_text: after jacob and his family returned from paddan-aram/mesopotamia, while they were still at bethel, god appeared to jacob again and blessed him.

source_text: the land that i promised to give to your grandfather abraham and your father isaac, i will give to you. i will also give it to your descendants.
target_text: rai dhu pangèd'u mi baki mu abraham, dènge ama mu isak, ja'a hia mi èu dènge ana-èpu èu.

source_text: when god finished talking there with jacob, he left him. jacob set up a large stone at the place where god had talked with him. he poured some wine and some olive oil on it to dedicate it to god.

source_text: jacob named that place bethel, which means ‘house of god', because god had spoken to him there.
target_text: era èèna, na pangare ‘betel'.

source_text: jacob and his family left bethel and traveled south toward ephrath town. when they were still some distance from ephrath, rachel began to have severe childbirth pains.
target_text: èle èèna ka, yakob si pakèd'i nèti betel. ropa rèngu kaj'èu èèna mèka nèti rae efrata nuka betlehem èèna, rahel dhu d'ai le lod'o nara iisi na. te ngaa nara iisi carui, hèia na roe titu kèna.

source_text: when her pain was the most severe, the ◄midwife/woman who helped her to give birth► said to rachel, do not be afraid, because now you have given birth to another son!

source_text: but she was dying, and with her last breath she said, name him benoni, which means ‘son of my sorrow', but his father named him benjamin, which means ‘son of my right hand'.
target_text: lod'o rahel oe ma'ète a'ae, na pangare ana ne, ben-oni, dhu sasoa na ‘ana nèti j'aj'èra ja'a'. ka heka na madhe kèna. te ngaa yakob hia ana ne ngara benyamin, dhu sasoa na ‘ana ai g'ana'.

source_text: after rachel died, she was buried alongside the road to ephrath, which is now called bethlehem.
target_text: ka ra padhane rahel ètu sebhe j'ara dhu la'e asa efrata, dhu limuri ne, ngara na betlehem.

source_text: jacob set up a large stone over her grave, and it is still there, showing where rachel's grave is.
target_text: hèia yakob pudhi lutu bhatu ètu ro'a dhèu èmu na èèna. d'ai sange ne'e, ro'a rahel ne era.

source_text: jacob, whose new name was israel, continued traveling with his family, and he set up his tents on the south side of the watchtower at eder town.
target_text: èle èèna ka, yakob pea boe mi ca era sa. ca tèka, na patitu paleo ètu sebhe manara eder.

source_text: while they were living in that area, jacob's son reuben had sex eup with bilhah, one of his father's ◄concubines/female slaves whom he had taken as a secondary wife►. someone told jacob about it, and it made him very angry. ◄i will now give you/here is► a list of jacob's twelve sons.
target_text: lod'o rèngu ètu era èèna, ruben j'unu dènge bilha, dhèu èmu piara ama na. èèna ka, yakob ne'a j'ara ne'e kahèi. ana mone yakob, canguru dua dhèu.

source_text: the sons of leah were reuben, who was jacob's oldest son, then simeon, levi, judah, issachar and zebulon.
target_text: ana-ana nèti lea, nuka: ruben ana uuru yakob, simeon, lewi, yahuda, isaskar, dènge sebulon.

source_text: the sons of rachel were joseph and benjamin.
target_text: ana-ana rahel, nuka: yusuf dènge benyamin.

source_text: the sons of rachel's female slave bilhah were dan and naphtali.
target_text: ana-ana nèti bilha, ènu rahel: dan dènge naftali.

source_text: the sons of leah's female slave zilpah were gad and asher. all those sons of jacob, except benjamin, were born while he was living in paddan-aram/mesopotamia.
target_text: aa ana-ana nèti silpa, ènu lea, nuka: gad dènge aser. rara iisi ana se ètu padan aram.

source_text: jacob had returned back home to see his father isaac at mamre, which is also named kiriath-arba, and which is now named hebron. isaac's father abraham had also lived there.
target_text: èle èèna ka, yakob la'e ngad'o ama na isak asa mamre, dhu dètu dènge kiryat-arba dhu limuri ne, ngara na hebron. uru èèna, baki na abraham pea ètu èèna.

source_text: isaac lived until he was 180 years old. he was very old when he died, joining his ancestors who had died previously. his sons esau and jacob buried his body.
target_text: umur isak d'ai ca ngasu aru nguru tèu, heka madhe kèna. ka ana na esau dènge yakob padhane ne.

source_text: ◄here is/i will now give you► a list of the descendants of esau, whose other name was edom.
target_text: ne'e ne, ana-èpu esau. ngara esau dhu leo, edom.

source_text: esau married three women from the canaan region: adah, the daughter of elon from the heth people-group; oholibamah, who was the daughter of anah and granddaughter of zibeon from the hiv people-group;
target_text: esau leo dènge ana bhèni kana'an dhèu dua. èci dhèu het, ana bhèni nèti elon, ngara na ada. dhèu èmu na èci hari, dhèu hewi, ngara na oholibama. ama na, ngara na anah, aa baki na sibeon.

source_text: and basemath, who was the daughter of ishmael and sister of nebaioth.
target_text: esau leo kahèi dènge ana ismael, ngara na basmat. ana mone basmat, ngara na nebayot.

source_text: esau's wife adah gave birth to eliphaz. basemath gave birth to reuel.
target_text: ada, dhèu èmu uuru esau, nara iisi elifas. basmat matana rahuel.

source_text: oholibamah gave birth to jeush, jalam, and korah. all these sons of esau were born while he was living in the canaan region.
target_text: aa oholibama matana yeus, yalam dènge kora. ana esau aa'i-aa'i ra sèra rara iisi si ètu rai kana'an.

source_text: jacob and esau had very many possessions. the result was that they needed more land for their livestock. the land where they were living was not big enough for both of them. they had too much livestock. so esau, whose other name was edom, had taken his wives and sons and daughters and all the other members of his household, his sheep and goats and his other animals, and all the other things he had obtained in canaan land, and they had moved to an area that was away from jacob.
target_text: ca tèka, esau pidha asa rai leo cue dhu kaj'èu nèti yakob. la'e nèti aa'i bhèni-ana niki, dhèu-dhèu sab'a, badha-manu, dènge mèdha-panyau na. esau pacèri dènge yakob, lula badha-manu ra dènge mèdha-panyau ra ae d'ai seli. nèti èèna ka, era pea rèngu katata ètu rai èèna.

source_text: they went to live in the seir hilly area.
target_text: hèia esau nuka edom la'e pea ètu ledhe ètu seir.

source_text: ◄here is/i will now give you► another list of the male descendants of esau. he was the ancestor of the edom people-group who live in the seir area.
target_text: se'e se, ana-èpu esau dhu ra peka na ‘dhèu edom'. rèngu pea ètu era ledhe seir.

source_text: esau's wife adah gave birth to eliphaz, and esau's wife basemath gave birth to reuel. the sons of eliphaz were teman, omar, zepho, gatam, and kenaz. esau's son eliphaz also had a ◄concubine/female slave whom he took as a secondary wife►. her name was timna. she gave birth to amalek. those six men were grandsons of esau's wife adah. reuel's sons were nahath, zerah, shammah, and mizzah. they were grandsons of esau's wife basemath.
target_text: ada, dhèu èmu esau, nara iisi ana mone ca dhèu, ngara na elifas. elifas ne, ana mone na, dhèu lèmi, nuka: teman, omar, sefo, gatam dènge kenas. dhèu èmu piara elifas, ngara na timna. nara iisi ana mone ca dhèu, ngara na amalek. dhèu èmu esau, basmat, nara iisi ana mone ca dhèu, ngara na rehuel. rehuel abhu ana mone dhèu èpa, nuka: nahat, sera, syama, dènge misa.

source_text: esau's wife oholibamah, who was the daughter of anah and granddaughter of zibeon, gave birth to three sons: jeush, jalam, and korah.
target_text: dhèu èmu esau, oholibama, ana nèti anah, aa èpu nèti sibeon, nara iisi ana mone dhèu tèlu, nuka: yeus, yalam, dènge kora.

source_text: ◄here is/i will now give you► a list of the people-groups who were descendants of esau. his oldest son eliphaz was the ancestor of the teman people-group, the omar people-group, the zepho people-group, the kenaz people-group, the korah people-group, the gatam people-group, and the amalek people-group. they were descendants of eliphaz and of esau's wife adah. they lived in the edom region.
target_text: ana-èpu esau se pahag'a lème, ka j'aj'i mi suku ae-ae. èci-èci ka dènge kapala suku ra. ana-ana elifas, dhu ana uuru nèti esau, j'aj'i kapala suku nèti suku teman, suku omar, suku sefo, suku kenas, suku kora, suku gatam dènge suku amalek. rèngu aa'i-aa'i se'e, ana-èpu nèti esau dènge dhèu èmu na ada.

source_text: the sons of esau's son reuel were ancestors of the nahath, zerah, shammah, and mizzah people-groups. they were descended from esau's wife basemath. they also lived in edom.
target_text: ana-ana rehuel, dhu ana nèti esau, j'aj'i kapala suku nèti suku nahat, suku sera, suku syama, dènge suku misa. aa'i-aa'i se, ana-èpu esau dènge dhèu èmu na, basmat.

source_text: the sons of esau's wife oholibamah, whose mother was anah, were ancestors of the jeush, jalam, and korah people-groups.
target_text: ana-ana nèti esau dènge dhèu èmu na, oholibama, j'aj'i kapala suku nèti suku yeus, suku yalam, dènge suku kora.

source_text: that is the list of the sons of esau, and the people-groups who were their descendants.
target_text: suku se'e aa'i-aa'i ra nèti ana-èpu esau.

source_text: ◄this is/i will now give you► a list of the descendants of seir, who belonged to the hor people-group, who were the first people-group who lived in the edom region: lotan, shobal, zibeon, anah, dishon, ezer, and dishan. those seven men became ancestors of people-groups. each of the people-groups had the same name as the name of their ancestor.
target_text: ètu era èèna, abhu dhèu hori èci, ngara na seir. ana-ana na pahag'a palème rai, ka j'aj'i suku ae-ae. èci-èci ka dènge kapala suku na. èle èèna ka, ana-ana na se j'aj'i kapala suku nèti suku lotan, suku sobal, suku sibeon, suku anah, suku dison, suku eser, dènge suku disan.

source_text: the sons of lotan were hori and heman and lotan's sister was timna.
target_text: ana lotan nuka: hori dènge heman. ana hèni lotan, nuka timna.

source_text: the sons of shobal were alvan, manahath, ebal, shepho, and onam.
target_text: ana-ana sobal, nuka: alwan, manahat, ebal, sefo, dènge onam.

source_text: the sons of zibeon were aiah and anah. this anah was the one who discovered the hot springs in the desert while he was taking care of his father zibeon's donkeys.
target_text: ana-ana nèti sibeon, nuka: aya, dènge anah. anah ne'e ka dhu rage madha èi pana ètu d'ara mamoo, lod'o na madhenga keled'ei ama na.

source_text: anah had two children-a son named dishon and a daughter named oholibamah. dishon's sons were hemdan, eshban, ithran, and keran.
target_text: ana bhèni nèti anah, nuka oholibama. aa ana mone na, nuka, dison. ana-ana dison, nuka: hemdan, esban, yitran, dènge keran.

source_text: ezer's sons were bilhan, zaavan, and akan.
target_text: ana-ana eser, nuka: bilhan, saawan, dènge akan.

source_text: dishan's sons were uz and aran.
target_text: ana-ana disan, nuka: us, dènge aran.

source_text: the people-groups who were descendants of hor lived in the seir/edom region. the names of the people-groups are lotan, shobal, zibeon, anah, dishon, ezer, and dishan.
target_text: de kapala-kapala suku nèti dhèu hori sèra, nuka: lotan, sobal, sibeon, anah, dison, eser, dènge disan. rèngu aa'i-aa'i se pea ètu rai seir.

source_text: these are the names of the kings who ruled in edom before any kings ruled over israel.
target_text: lod'o dhu kabarai isra'el dènge mèka dhèu aae, te ngaa ètu rai edom dènge le dhèu aae. ngara dhèu aae se, dhutu-dhutu, nuka:

source_text: beor's son bela became the first king in edom. the city where he lived was named dinhabah.
target_text: ra ded'e bela, ana nèti beor, j'aj'i dhèu aae ètu kota dinhaba.

source_text: when bela died, zerah's son jobab/became the king. he was from bozrah city.
target_text: ropa bela madhe, ra ded'e yobab ho gati ne, j'aj'i dhèu aae. ama na, ngara na sera, nèti rae bosra.

source_text: when jobab died, husham became the king. he was from the region where the teman people-group lived.
target_text: ropa yobab madhe, ra ded'e husam ho gati na, j'aj'i dhèu aae. husam ne, nèti rai dhèu teman.

source_text: when husham died, bedad's son hadan became the king. husham's army fought the army of the midian people-group in the moab region and defeated them. the city where husham lived was avith.
target_text: ropa husam madhe, ra ded'e hadad ho gati na, j'aj'i dhèu aae. ama na, ngara na bedad, nèti rae awit. nèngu ka dhu segi dhèu midian, lod'o ra pamusu ètu moab.

source_text: when hadad died, samlah became the king. he was from masrekah town.
target_text: ropa hadad madhe, ra ded'e samla ho gati na, j'aj'i dhèu aae. nèngu ne, nèti rae masreka.

source_text: when samlah died, shaul became the king. he was from rehoboth town along the euphrates river.
target_text: ropa samla madhe, ra ded'e saul ho gati na, j'aj'i dhèu aae. saul èèna, nèti rae rehobot, dhu ètu sebhe loko.

source_text: when shaul died, achbor's son baal-hanan became king.
target_text: ropa saul madhe, ra ded'e baal-hanan ho gati na, j'aj'i dhèu aae. ama na, ngara na akbor.

source_text: when achbor's son baal-hanan died, hadad became king. the city where he lived was named pau. his wife's name was mehetabel. she was the daughter of matred, who was the daughter of me-zahab.
target_text: ropa baal-hanan madhe, ra ded'e hadar ho gati na, j'aj'i dhèu aae. hadar ne, nèti rae pau. aa dhèu èmu na, ngara mehetabel. ama mehetabel, ngara na matret. aa baki na, mesahab.

source_text: ◄here is/i will now give you► a list of all the people-groups that were descendants of esau: timna, alvah, jetheth, oholibamah, elah, pinon, kenaz, teman, mibzar, magdiel, and iram. they all lived in the edom region. the land where each people-group lived got the same name as the name of the people-group.
target_text: de kapala-kapala suku dhu j'aj'i nèti ana-èpu esau, nuka: timna, alwa, yetet, oholibama, ela, pinon, kenas, teman, mibsar, magdiel, dènge iram. rèngu se èci-èci pangare rai ra madhutu ngara rèngu unu ra. de aa'i-aa'i se'e, lii lolo nèti ana-èpu esau, dhèu edom èèna.

source_text: jacob continued to live in the canaan region where his father had lived previously.
target_text: ne'e ne, lii lole nèti yakob si. ca tèka ka, yakob la'e pea hari asa rai kana'an. èèna, era pea ama na isak nèti uru ka.

source_text: ◄this is/i will now tell you► what happened to jacob's family. when his son joseph was 17 years old, he was taking care of the flocks of sheep and goats with some of his older brothers. they were sons of his father's ◄concubines/female slaves that he had taken to be his secondary wives►. joseph sometimes told his father about bad things that his brothers were doing.
target_text: tèu èèna, ana yakob èci, nèti dhèu èmu na rahel, ngara na yusuf. yusuf ne'e, ropa umur na d'ai canguru pidhu tèu, nèngu dènge a'a na si, tema le j'aga kahib'i-kalèbho rèngu. a'a na sèra, ana nèti ina leo hari, ngara na bilha dènge silpa. te ngaa yusuf ne'e tuka tenge lii mi dedha a'a na si, ho la'e pana'e ama na.

source_text: jacob loved joseph more than he loved any of his other children, because joseph had been born when jacob was an old man. jacob made for joseph a long pretty robe that had long sleeves.
target_text: lod'o dhu rara iisi yusuf na, ama na dhu heka le. nèti èèna ka, na sue yusuf ne risi eele nèti ana-ana na leo sèra. ca lod'o ka, yakob j'au kodho madhera èci dhu saraga bia hia yusuf.

source_text: when joseph's older brothers realized that their father loved him more than he loved any of them, they hated him. they never spoke kindly to him.
target_text: ropa a'a na si ladhe-ladhe la'a na ama na sue risi yusuf, hèia ra mulai tèka d'ara dènge ne, ro'o boe padhai lii dènge ne.

source_text: one night joseph had a dream. he told his brothers about the dream. he said to them, listen to the dream i had! in the dream, we were tying up bundles of wheat in the field. suddenly my bundle stood up straight, and surprisingly, your bundles gathered around my bundle and bowed down to it!
target_text: mèda ca lod'o ka yusuf nii. kèd'i nèti bhèj'i ka, na lolo dènge a'a na si lii nii deo na, aku nèngu na, we! mi nanene ku la! ja'a nii, na èdhi aa'i-aa'i ti, èki are ètu d'ara oka. kabèdhi laa, are dhu ja'a èki titu dhoo-dhoo. te ngaa are miu, oke mere are ja'a deo na, ka pacud'u mi unu ja'a. ra nanene rare sèmi èèna, hèia a'a na se'e tabha nasa hari dènge ne.

source_text: his brothers said to him, do you think that some day you will rule over us? are you saying that some day you are going to be our king? rhq they hated him even more than before because of what he had told them about his dream.
target_text: hèia ra jèke ne, aku rèngu na, we! èu ngee na, èu neo j'aj'i dhèu kapai kèna, ho neo paredha ji'i, do? taga na lolo lii nii ne'e, hèia asa ra nasa dènge ne.

source_text: later he had another dream, and again he told his older brothers about it. he said, listen to this! i had another dream. in this dream, the sun and moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me!
target_text: nèbhu boe, yusuf nii hari ca tèka. na lolo hari dènge a'a na si, aku nèngu na, we! ja'a nii hari, sèmi ne'e ka. ja'a kèdhi madha lod'o, hèru, dènge hua-hètu canguru èci. aa'i-aa'i sèra, pahaha iisi mi ja'a.

source_text: he also told his father about it. his father rebuked him, saying what are you suggesting by that dream rhq? do you think it means that your mother and i and your older brothers will some day bow down to the ground in front of you? rhq
target_text: hèia yusuf lolo hari lii nii deo na dènge ama na, aa dènge a'a na sèra. ka ama na jèke ne, aku nèngu na, lii nii ngaa, kèna! èu ngee na, ja'a dènge ina mu, dènge a'ari èu sèra, mai uu kabaj'èla èu, do? èu nia ae le èèna, nga!

source_text: joseph's older brothers were furious/angry with him, but his father just kept thinking about what the dream meant.
target_text: nèti èèna ka, a'a na sèra tèka d'ara bia dènge ne. te ngaa ama na pangee taruu lii nii èèna ètu d'ara na.

source_text: one day joseph's older brothers went to take care of their father's sheep and goats that were eating grass near shechem.
target_text: ca tèka ka, a'a yusuf sèra rèti kahib'i-kalèbho ama na, asa era j'u'u dètu dènge rae sikem.

source_text: some time later, jacob said to joseph, your brothers are taking care of the sheep and goats near shechem rhq. i am going to send you there to see them. joseph replied, okay.
target_text: nèbhu boe ka, ama na peka dènge yusuf, aku nèngu na, a'a mu si j'aga kahib'i-kalèbho dètu dènge sikem. de èu pa'èra, ho lamu ladhe ku si la. ka yusuf dhaa, aku nèngu na, ja'a laku, ama.

source_text: jacob said, go and see if they are doing okay, and if the flocks are doing okay. then come back and give me a report. so jacob sent joseph from the valley where they were living, the valley where hebron is located, to go north to find his brothers. when joseph arrived near shechem city,
target_text: hèia ama na peka hari, aku nèngu na, èu lamu ladhe a'a mu si, dènge kahib'i-kalèbho èdhi. ladhe ra samia na, mai peka dènge ja'a. ka yusuf pakèd'i ka nèti d'ara pad'a hebron, la'e taruu d'ai sikem.

source_text: while he was wandering around in the fields looking/searching for his brothers, a man saw him and asked him, whom are you looking/searching for?
target_text: d'ai nèi, na tenge a'a na si, palème d'ara pad'a èèna. na paraga dènge dhèu mone èci, ka dhèu èèna karèi ne, aku nèngu na, èu tenge ngaa?

source_text: joseph replied, i am looking for my older brothers. can you tell me where they are taking care of their sheep and goats?
target_text: yusuf dhaa, aku nèngu na, ja'a tenge a'a ja'a. rèngu eo kahib'i-kalèbho dètu ètu era ne'e. de ama, èu paraga dènge si, do aad'o?

source_text: the man replied, they are not here any more. i heard one of them saying, ‘let's take the sheep and goats and go to dothan town. ' so joseph left there and went north, and found his older brothers near dothan.
target_text: hèia, dhèu deo na peka, aku nèngu na, ra aad'o heka ètu ne'e. te ja'a tadèngi, ra peka na lasi padètu dènge rae dotan. hèia yusuf la'e taruu, ka paraga dènge si ètu rae dotan.

source_text: but they saw him when he was still far away, and they decided to kill him.
target_text: ropa ladhe rèdhi yusuf nèti kaj'èu, ra padhue rare lii èci neo pamadhe ne.

source_text: they said to each other things like, here comes that dreamer!
target_text: èci peka dènge èci, aku rèngu na, miu ladhe ku la! mone eele tuka nii na, nuka mai nèi!

source_text: and hey, let's kill him, and then throw his body into one of the pits/cisterns. then we will tell people that a ferocious/wild animal attacked and killed him and ate him. and then we will ◄find out whether his dreams come true/make sure that his dreams do not come true►!
target_text: de mai ho ti pamadhe ne. ho èèna na, ti core eele ne asa d'ara madha èi madhe èèna. ladhe d'ai èmu na, ti peka dènge ama peka na, badha hui ra'e ne. ho èèna na, ti ladhe sèku, lii nii na sèra sa mia!

source_text: reuben heard what they were saying, so he tried to persuade them not to kill mty joseph. he said, no, we should not kill him.
target_text: ropa nanene èèna, hèia a'a na ruben tenge j'ara ho patabuli eele yusuf. hèia na kai ari na si, aku nèngu na, we! èdhi baku pamadhe ne!

source_text: do not even shed his blood! we can throw him into this pit/cistern in the desert, but we should not harm him mty. he said that, and then left them, planning to rescue joseph later and take him back to his father.
target_text: be'a risi èdhi kèpe ne, ti tao asa d'ara madha èi madhe nèi. ètu èèna, era dhu dhèu aad'o, de èci sa rèdhi boe ne. sad'i baku pasuti raa na. na peka sèmi èèna, lula na tenge j'ara ho patalale yusuf, ho hia na lèpa hari èmu.

source_text: so when joseph arrived where his older brothers were, they seized him and ripped off his pretty robe with long sleeves.
target_text: ropa yusuf d'ai madha a'a na si, ra kèpe ne, ka ra rèbhi eele kodho dhu saraga aae ètu ua na.

source_text: then they took him and threw him into the pit/cistern. but the pit/cistern was dry; there was no water in it.
target_text: ka ra nuni pa'oro ne, hèia ra tule ne asa d'ara madha èi madhe èèna.

source_text: after they sat down to eat some food, they looked up and saw a ◄caravan/group of traders►, descendants of ishmael, coming from the gilead area. their camels were loaded with bags of spices and nice-smelling resins. they were going down to egypt to sell those things there.
target_text: èle èèna ka, ra lèpa, lasi ra'a-rinu. ètu talora ra'a-rinu, kabèdhi la ra ladhe rèdhi dhèu canau mai re èèna. dhèu sèra kako rèti dènge badha onta ra, hue dènge mèdha d'aga, sèmi raa aj'u hèu mèngi, bubhu-bubhu dènge èi na'i rupa-rupa. dhèu sèra sa, dhèu ismael, dhu mai nèti rae gilead neo lasi kaj'èu d'ai masir.

source_text: she called the household servants. she said to them, look! this hebrew man that my husband brought to us is ◄insulting/trying to do something disgraceful to► us! he came into my room and tried to ◄rape me/make me have sex eup with him►, but i screamed loudly. as soon as he heard me scream loudly, he left his loincloth with me and ran outside!
target_text: hèia na paroa dhèu sab'a sèra, ka na peka, aku nèngu na, we! miu mai ladhe ku laa! deo na, ana mone dhèu ibrani na, maso sa d'ara kama ja'a. na neo pamakae ja'a. malo ka ja'a pa'oo, ka na rai, tèke eele kodho na ètu ja'a ne. dhèu èmu ja'a ne, nèti dhèu bhelu asa d'ara èmu, ho hia èdhi ta'e makae!

source_text: she kept the loincloth beside her until her husband, joseph's master, came home.
target_text: bhèni na kèpe pa'ère kodho èèna, toke d'ai dhèu èmu na lèpa.

source_text: then she told him this story: that hebrew slave whom you brought here came into my room and tried to rape me!
target_text: ropa dhèu èmu na nare d'ara èmu, na lolo peka na, a'a! dhèu ibrani dhu mèti mai sa èmu ne'e, deo na maso asa d'ara kama ja'a, neo pakarehe ja'a!

source_text: as soon as i screamed loudly, he ran outside, leaving me holding his loincloth!
target_text: malo ka ja'a pa'oo, paroa ana sab'a se'e. hèia na rai tèke eele kodho na, ka ne'e.

source_text: when joseph's master heard this story that his wife told him, saying this is how your slave treated me, he was very angry.
target_text: tadèngi nare lii lolo dhèu èmu na, potifar nasa bia.

source_text: joseph's master took joseph and put him in prison, the place where all the king's prisoners were put, and joseph stayed there.
target_text: hèia na paredha ka dhèu lasi kèpe yusuf. ka ra pamaso asa d'ara bèdho dhèu aae.

source_text: but yahweh was kind to joseph and helped him, and caused the ◄prison warden/man who was in charge of the prison► to be pleased with him.
target_text: te ngaa lamatua bhèlu boe yusuf. nèti èèna ka, lamatua ladhe-leru ne taruu, ka kapala ètu d'ara bèdho èèna, sue yusuf ae titu kèna.

source_text: so the prison warden put joseph in charge of all those who were in the prison, and in charge of all the work that was done there.
target_text: na lèka yusuf, ka hia ne j'aj'i madho ho laladhe ana bèdho sèra aa'i-aa'i ra. aa, hia na lalau sasab'a ètu èèna kahèi.

source_text: the warden was not concerned with anything that joseph was taking care of, because yahweh helped joseph to do well everything that he did.
target_text: lula lèka ne, ka kapala èmu bèdho na, tao heka ai-hèb'a mi ngaa-ngaa ètu d'ara bèdho èèna. lamatua ladhe-leru taruu yusuf, nèti èèna ka, sasab'a ngaa ètu d'ara bèdho na kako dènge be'a.

source_text: some time later, two of the king of egypt's officials did things that displeased him. one was his chief ◄drink-server/man who prepared the wine and served it to the king►, and the other was his chief ◄baker/man who baked bread for the king►. the king became angry with both of them. so he had them put in prison, in the house of the captain of the palace guards. that was the place where joseph was being kept.
target_text: ètu d'ara bèdho èèna, abhu kahèi dhèu dua, dhu uru na j'aj'i kapala urusan ètu d'ara èmu dhèu aae masir. èci lalau dhua èi dhèu aae. aa èci hari lalau roti dhèu aae. dua ra tao pasala dhèu aae. nèti èèna ka, dhèu aae nasa, ka na pamaso si asa d'ara bèdho. dua ra pea ètu era èci dènge yusuf.

source_text: the two men were in prison for a long time. and during that time the captain of the palace guards appointed joseph to be their servant, to take care of their needs.
target_text: kapala èmu bèdho na, paredha yusuf lalau dhèu dua se'e. ra ètu d'ara bèdho na, ele boe ca tèu do dua tèu le.

source_text: one night while the king's drink-server and his baker were there in the prison, each of them had a dream. each dream had a different meaning.
target_text: mèda ca lod'o ka, dua ra nii. ca dhèu ka dènge nii na. aa, lii nii dua sèra, èci-èci ka dènge sasoa na.

source_text: the next morning, when joseph came to them, he saw that both of them were dejected/worried.
target_text: bèli mad'ae èèna, yusuf ladhe na dua ra rèhu susa.

source_text: so he asked them, why do you look so sad today?
target_text: ka na karèi si, aku nèngu na, nga tao ka mad'ae ne'e, miu dua mi roe-roe?

source_text: one of them answered, we both had dreams last night, but there is no one who can tell us the meaning of the dreams. joseph said to them, god is the only one who can rhq tell the meaning of dreams. so tell me what you dreamed, and god will tell me the meaning.
target_text: hèia ra dhaa, peka na, mèda deo na, ji'i nii. te ngaa ji'i nge'a boe sasoa na samia! hèia yusuf peka dènge dua ra, aku nèngu na, dhèu aa'i-aa'i ètu rai-haha ne'e, èci sa re'a boe sasoa nii, dhodhoka ama lamatua di. de miu lolo ku laa. pe èèna ho ja'a karèi sasoa nèti lamatua.

source_text: so the king's chief drink-server told his dream to joseph. he said, in my dream i saw a grapevine in front of me.
target_text: hèia dhèu dhu lalau dhua èi hia dhèu aae èèna, lolo uuru peka na, ètu d'ara nii, ja'a ladhe kèdhi aj'u anggor ca kapua.

source_text: on the vine there were three branches. after the branches budded, they blossomed, and then they produced clusters of grapes.
target_text: aj'u anggor ne dadana nèngu tèlu di. aj'u na muri mai ka dènge rèu, hela, dènge hua giru-gari dhu madhasa.

source_text: i was holding the king's cup, so i took the grapes and squeezed the juice into the cup. then i gave the cup to the king to drink the juice.
target_text: aa ja'a kèd'u galaa dhu dhèu aae biasa pake ninu. ja'a puu hua anggor, ka pacèli èi sa d'ara galaa deo na. hèia kèti asa dhèu aae, hia na ninu.

source_text: god immediately told joseph what the dream meant. so joseph said to him, this is the meaning of your dream: the three branches of the vine represent three days.
target_text: tadèngi nare hèia, yusuf peka dènge ne sèmi ne'e ka, ama, ee. sasoa nii na sèmi ne'e ka: dadana tèlu, sasoa na di tèlu lod'o ka.

source_text: within three days the king will release you from prison. he will let you do the work that you did before. you will take cups of wine to the king as you did before, when you were his drink-server.
target_text: ètu d'ara tèlu lod'o ne, dhèu aae kalua eele ama nèti d'ara bèdho ne'e. ho na hia hari, ama lalau dhua èi hia dhèu aae sèmi uru na.

source_text: but when you are out of prison and everything goes well for you, please do not forget me.
target_text: ladhe ama abhu babe'a sèmi èèna, baku bhèlu ja'a, ee? ladhe ama sue ja'a, peka dènge dhèu aae kalua eele ja'a nèti era ne'e.

source_text: people took me away forcefully from the land where my fellow hebrews live. i did nothing wrong there, and also while i have been here in egypt, i have done nothing for which i deserved to be put in prison. so be kind to me and tell the king about me, so that he will release me from this prison!
target_text: te ja'a ne, madhutu madha j'ara na dhu mola, rèngu se rare ja'a dènge laka-seti, nèti rae dhèu ibrani. d'ai era ne'e, ja'a tao boe sasala ngaa èci sa. te ngaa rèngu pamaso ja'a asa d'ara bèdho ne'e. rèngu tao ja'a sèmi dhèu bhelu-katub'a sa.

source_text: when the chief baker heard that the meaning of the dream of the king's drink-server was very favorable, he said to joseph, i also had a dream. in the dream i was surprised to see three baskets of bread stacked on my head.
target_text: ropa tadèngi nare sasoa nii ne'e be'a mi dedha angalai na, hèia dhèu èci dhu lalau roti na, lolo hari nii nèngu, peka na, ari yusuf. nii ja'a sèmi ne'e ka: ja'a tèd'u soe pagod'o-god'o tèlu.

source_text: in the top basket there were many kinds of baked goods for the king, but birds were eating them from the top basket that was on my head!
target_text: ètu d'ara soe re dedha tèka na, pènu dènge koki dhèu aae, dhu rupa ae titu kèna. te ngaa manu-bhui lela mai ka ra'e aa'i koki d'ara soe dhu ètu kètu ja'a na.

source_text: god again told joseph what the dream meant, so he said, the three baskets also represent three days.
target_text: ropa yusuf tadèngi nare, ka na dhaa, peka na, sasoa lii nii ama, sèmi ne'e ka: soe tèlu sèra, sama kahèi dènge tèlu lod'o.

source_text: within three days the king will command that your head be cut off. then your body will be hung on a tree, and vultures will come and eat your flesh.
target_text: d'ara tèlu lod'o ne, mu ladhe, te dhèu aae pua dhèu mai poro rare kètu èu. ho èèna na, ra kadhoe ngi'u aae èu ètu agarii. hèia manu-bhui tutu ra'e aa'i sisi èu.

source_text: the third day after that was the ◄king's birthday/day they celebrated when the king became one year older►. on that day the king invited all his officials to celebrate his birthday. during the celebration, while they were all gathered there, the king summoned his chief drink-server and chief baker from the prison.
target_text: ropa d'ai tèlu lod'o, dhu lèke dènge lod'o hari jadi dhèu aae, na tao tatao dhu kapai hia dhèu kapai na aa'i-aa'i sèra. na paredha ho dhèu lasi kalua eele dhèu dua sèra nèti d'ara bèdho.

source_text: he said that his chief drink-server could have his previous job again, so that again he took cups of wine to the king.
target_text: ka na hia hari mone dhu lalau dhua èi na, sab'e sasab'a nèngu uru na.

source_text: but he commanded that the chief baker should be killed by being hanged, just as joseph had said would happen when he told the two men the meaning of their dreams.
target_text: te ngaa dhèu dhu lalau roti dhèu aae èèna, ra poro eele kètu na, ka ra kadhoe ngi'u na, sama sèmi ngaa dhu yusuf peka dènge rèngu dua ra.

source_text: but the chief drink-server did not think about joseph. he forgot to do what joseph asked him to do.
target_text: te ngaa mone dhu lalau dhua èi dhèu aae ne, sanèd'e heka yusuf. na bhèlu eele lii moa yusuf.

source_text: two complete years later, the king of egypt had a dream. in the dream, he was standing alongside the nile river.
target_text: pe d'ai dua tèu risi sa, hèia dhèu aae masir nii. na nii na, nèngu dhu titu ètu sebhe loko nil.

source_text: suddenly seven healthy fat cows come up out of the river. they started eating the grass that was on the riverbank.
target_text: kabèdhi laa, nèngu nèdhi sapi pidhu ngi'u dhu kabèb'u bia. ka'uri ra kale'e. ra kalua nèti d'ara loko, ka ra'a j'u'u ètu sebhe loko èèna.

source_text: soon seven other cows, unhealthy-looking and thin, came up behind them from the nile river. they stood alongside the fat cows that were on the riverbank.
target_text: nèbhu boe, sapi pidhu ngi'u dhu leo hari, kalua nèti d'ara loko deo na. ngi'u sapi sèra malaka-god'a. ra titu padètu dènge sapi kabèb'u sèra.

source_text: then the unhealthy thin cows ate the seven healthy fat cows. and then the king woke up.
target_text: hèia sapi malaka pidhu ngi'u sèra, dhèle aa'i pidhu sapi dhu kabèb'u sèra. hèia dhèu aae kabèdhi, ka na marèi dènge.

source_text: the king went to sleep again, and he had another dream. this time he saw seven heads of grain that were full of kernels of grain and ripe, and all growing on one stalk.
target_text: nèbhu boe ka, dhèu aae bhèj'i luu hari. ka na nii hari ca tèka. lii nii na sèmi ne'e ka: nèngu ladhe nèdhi are pidhu huri dhu isi pènu, bhodho nèti laa are dhu sub'u.

source_text: after that, the king saw that seven other heads of grain sprouted on that or, on another stalk. they were thin and had been dried up by the hot east wind.
target_text: èle èèna ka, nèdhi hari are pidhu huri dhu isi aad'o, aa dhu kamale dhae-dhae sène, lèke lai ngèlu dhu pana.

source_text: then the thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven ripe full heads. then the king woke up. he realized that he had been dreaming.
target_text: ka pidhu huri are dhu isi aad'o sèra, dhèle aa'i pidhu huri are dhu isi pènu deo sa. hèia dhèu aae kabèdhi ka nèti bhèj'i. heka nèngu ne'a kèna, nèngu dhu nii hari di.

source_text: but the next morning he was worried about the meaning of the dream. so he summoned all the magicians and wise men who lived in egypt. he told them what he had dreamed, but none of them could tell him the meaning of the two dreams.
target_text: mad'ae aae èèna, d'ara isi na be'a boe. hèia, na paredha dhèu lasi paroa aa'i dhèu ai tadha dènge dhèu d'èlu-mèu, ètu rai masir mai paraga dènge ne. ka na lolo lii nii na sèra dènge si. te ngaa dhèu èci sa bisa boe peka sasoa lii nii deo sa mi dhèu aae.

source_text: then the chief drink-server said to the king, now i remember something that i should have told you! i made a mistake by forgetting to tell it to you.
target_text: ka mone dhu lalau dhua èi dhèu aae èèna, heka sanèd'e nèdhi yusuf kèna. hèia la'e peka dènge dhèu aae, aku nèngu na, ama! ja'a mangaku sala.

source_text: one time you were angry with two of us. so you put me and the chief baker in the prison in the house of the captain of the palace guards.
target_text: uru èèna, dhu ama ku nasa dènge ja'a, dènge angalai ku èci na, ka pamaso ji'i asa d'ara bèdho,

source_text: while we were there, one night each of us had a dream, and the dreams had different meanings.
target_text: mèda ca lod'o ka, ji'i dua mi nii. èci-èci ka dènge nii na. aa sasoa nii se'e, sama boe kahèi.

source_text: there was a young hebrew man there with us. he was a servant of the captain of the palace guards. we told him what we had dreamed, and he told us what our dreams meant. he told each of us the meaning of our dreams.
target_text: ètu d'ara bèdho na, abhu ana mone ibrani èci. kapala èmu bèdho nedhe ana mone ne, j'aj'i kapala urusan ho lalau ji'i. ji'i lolo lii nii ji'i dènge ne, ka na peka sasoa lii nii sèra dènge ji'i.

source_text: and what happened was exactly the same as the meanings that he told us: you said i could have my previous job again, but the other man was killed by being hanged. the hebrew man's name was joseph.
target_text: nèti èèna ka, ama dhèu aae ded'e hari ja'a. aa angalai ja'a na, abhu huku madhe. se'e se j'aj'i sama sèmi ngaa dhu ana mone ibrani na peka.

source_text: when the king heard that, he told some servants to bring joseph to him, and they quickly brought joseph out of the prison. joseph shaved and put on better clothes, and then he went and stood in front of the king.
target_text: nanene nare lii ne'e hèia, dhèu aae pua dhèu lasi lai-lai rare yusuf nèti d'ara bèdho mai. ka yusuf pamèu iisi na, aa na gati mèdha-papake na, ka na la'e paraga dènge dhèu aae.

source_text: the king said to joseph, i had two dreams, and no one can tell me what they mean. but someone told me that when you hear someone tell about a dream he has had, you can tell that person what the dream means.
target_text: ropa na d'ai madha hèia, dhèu aae peka, ja'a nii, te ngaa dhèu èci sa re'a boe sasoa lii nii sèra. te ngaa dhèu peka na èu me'a.

source_text: but joseph replied to the king, no, i cannot do that. it is god who knows the meaning of dreams, but he will enable me to tell you their meaning, and they will mean something good.
target_text: hèia yusuf dhaa, aku nèngu na, ama dhèu aae. ja'a èèna ka oo, ke'a boe ngaa-ngaa kahèi. dhoka ama lamatua di dhu ne'a, ho na peka sasoa lii nii sa, dènge lèke. na neo peka lii dhu be'a mi ama dhèu aae.

source_text: the king said to joseph, in my first dream i was standing on the bank of the nile river.
target_text: hèia dhèu aae lolo ka, lii nii sèra dènge ne, aku nèngu na, ètu d'ara nii èèna, ja'a titu ètu sebhe loko nil.

source_text: suddenly seven healthy fat cows came up out of the river, and they started eating the grass that was on the riverbank.
target_text: ja'a ladhe la'a na sapi pidhu ngi'u dhu kabèb'u bia, dènge ka'uri dhu kale'e. ra kalua nèti d'ara loko mai, ka ra'a j'u'u ètu sebhe loko èèna.

source_text: soon seven other cows, ugly and thin ones, came up behind them from the river. i never saw such ugly cows in all the land of egypt!
target_text: hèia sapi pidhu ngi'u dhu leo mai hari. rèngu se'e dhu malaka-god'a. ètu rai masir ne'e, ja'a kèdhi mèka sapi dhu malaka-god'a sèmi èèna!

source_text: the thin ugly cows ate the seven fat cows that came up first.
target_text: dhu pamalaa ja'a, pidhu sapi dhu malaka-god'a sèra, kabèdhi laa dhèle aa'i pidhu sapi dhu kabèb'u se.

source_text: but afterwards, no one would have known that the thin cows ate them, because they were just as ugly as they were before. then i woke up.
target_text: sapi dhu malaka sèra dhèle aa'i, te ngaa ngi'u ra malaka taruu sèmi èèna ka. hèia ja'a kabèdhi dènge ka.

source_text: then i had another dream. i saw seven heads of grain. they were full of kernels of grain and ripe, and they were all growing on one stalk.
target_text: èle èèna ka, ja'a bhèj'i luu hari, ka nii hari ca tèka. ja'a kèdhi pidhu huri are dhu isi pènu, kalua nèti laa are ca kapua dhu sub'u.

source_text: then to my surprise i saw seven other heads of grain that sprouted. they were thin and had been dried up by the hot east wind.
target_text: èle èèna ka, ja'a kèdhi hari, pidhu huri are dhu isi aad'o, aa dhu kamale dhae-dhae, lèke lai ngèlu pana.

source_text: the thin heads of grain swallowed the seven good heads. i told these dreams to the magicians, but none of them could explain to me what they meant.
target_text: ka pidhu huri are dhu bèdhu sèra dhèle aa'i pidhu huri are dhu isi pènu sèra. èle èèna ka, ja'a kèd'i nèti bhèj'i. ka ja'a lolo lii nii se'e mi dhèu d'èlu-mèu se'e, te ngaa èci sa bisa boe peka sasoa lii nii sèra.

source_text: then joseph said to the king, both your dreams have the same meaning. god is revealing to you in your dreams what he is about to do.
target_text: hèia yusuf padhai lii, peka na, ama dhèu aae! lii nii dua sèra, sasoa na dhoka èci di. ama lamatua peka le, mi ama dhèu aae, ngaa dhu na neo tao.

source_text: the seven healthy cows represent seven years. the seven good heads of grain also represent seven years. the two dreams both have the same meaning.
target_text: sasoa na sèmi ne'e ka: pidhu sapi dhu kabèb'u, dènge pidhu huri are dhu isi pènu sèra, sasoa na, tèu dhu bècu-manèsa pidhu tèu. sasoa ra dhoka èci di.

source_text: the seven thin ugly cows that came up behind them and the seven worthless heads of grain that were dried up by the hot east wind each represent seven years ◄of famine/when food will be very scarce►.
target_text: sèmi èèna kahèi, pidhu sapi dhu malaka-god'a, dènge pidhu huri are dhu isi aad'o, sasoa na, tèu manganga pidhu tèu.

source_text: it will happen just as i have told you, because god has revealed to you what he is about to do.
target_text: de lamatua dhu peka mema le, ngaa dhu nèngu neo tao. èèna sama kahèi, dènge ngaa dhu ja'a peka deo na.

source_text: there will be seven years in which there will be plenty of food throughout the land of egypt,
target_text: ladhe bèli-camèd'a, ètu rai masir ne'e, d'ara pidhu tèu, èdhi abhu bècu-manèsa palème rae.

source_text: but after that there will be seven years ◄of famine/when food will be very scarce►. then people will forget all the years when there was plenty of food, because the famine that will come afterward will ruin the country. the people will forget how plentiful food was previously, because the famine will be very terrible.
target_text: èle èèna na, heka èdhi abhu manganga d'ara pidhu tèu. d'ara pidhu tèu na, manganga madèu aae. toke èdhi abhu boe nganga'a calamusi sa, ètu dedha rai masir ne'e. dhèu aa'i-aa'i manganga ae titu kèna, ka ra bhèlu eele uru na dhu rèngu abhu le babècu pidhu tèu.

source_text: the reason god gave to you two dreams is that he wants you to know that this will happen, and he will cause it to happen very soon.
target_text: de ladhe ama dhèu aae abhu nii dua hari, sasoa na, ama lamatua ka dhu ator tèke. nèbhu heka, ngaa dhu na ator ne, j'aj'i kèna.

source_text: now i suggest that you should choose a man who is wise and can make good decisions. i suggest that you appoint him to direct the affairs of the whole country.
target_text: nèti èèna ka, ja'a manèngi sèmi ne'e: be'a risi ama dhèu aae tenge dhèu d'èlu-mèu èci, dhu bisa tao ai-hèb'a la'a dènge be'a. aa ded'e ne, ho ladhe-leru kabarai ne'e dènge be'a.

source_text: you should also appoint supervisors over the country, in order that they can arrange to collect one-fifth of all the grain that is harvested during the seven years when food is plentiful.
target_text: d'ara pidhu tèu dhu bècu èèna, be'a risi ama dhèu aae ded'e hari dhèu, ho ra oru-pakaboko nganga'a dhu risi eele. nganga'a dhu risi sèra, bagi mi lèmi ho tèke ca pala.

source_text: they should collect this amount of grain during those seven years that are coming, when there will be plenty of food. you should supervise them as they store it in the cities.
target_text: ana kabarai ne'e, hud'i madhutu dènge be'a paredha ama dhèu aae, ho pakaboko are-are dhu risi eele, nèti rae-rae ètu rai masir ne'e. aa ra soli sa d'ara soka ho j'aga paie.

source_text: this grain should be stored so that it can be eaten during the seven years when there will be a famine here in egypt, so that the people in this country will not die from hunger.
target_text: sèna ka pidhu tèu dhu manganga nèi mai te, èdhi dhu sadia le nganga'a. dènge j'ara sèmi ne'e, èci sa madhe boe manganga.

source_text: the king and his officials thought that this would be a good plan.

source_text: but they told him everything that joseph had said to them, and jacob saw the carts that joseph had sent to carry him and his family and possessions to egypt. then their father jacob's shock ended.
